Never again will my people be victims."_

[[Cadmus Tacet]] is born as an [[Underdog]] and is one of the most important figures of [[Arcanoria]]. He is the very first person to coin the term [[Age of Humanity]] properly during [[Ages]] V and proposes that [[Humanity]] must forge its own future through the ruthless pursuit of progress. He is very devout to the [[Auric Aria]] and believes that truth and safety can only come from the scalpel of human reason and its creator.

The core philosophy of [[Cadmus Tacet]] cements during his childhood after being witness to the tyrannical oppression of draconic [[Pure Light]] beings who subjugated and enslaved the human populace on the region he was born. Treating human sacrifice as tribute and livestock.

The words of the [[Age of Humanity]] engraved in his mind by witnessing the execution of a man whose name he never knew yet would never forget his last words, vowing to make it a prophecy:

  - "Poor little, human. Too small to even serve a snack. Face it, you are weak, and you will always be the subject of the [[Pure Light]] rule forever while your kind cowers in the grass." - Demi Human Dragon executor.
  - "I swear, by my last breath, that one day... a reckoning will come. [[Humanity]] will outlast every single one of you, and your very essence shall become the fuel on which the sons of my sons will run. And then you will see, for that will be the [[Age of Humanity]]."
  - "Is that insolence your last words? Pathetic." The executor says as he impaled the neck of the man with a [[Crystal]] spear.

[[Cadmus Tacet]] is then driven in exile to escape the very same fate of this man, and makes a desperate search of anything that would make him question what do [[Pure Light]] beings have that [[Humanity]] does not. He awakens his [[Motif Awakening]] on the search of the truth beneath what could be the structure that makes [[Humanity]] outlast these very executors that treated [[Humanity]] as livestock and slaves.

He then goes on an expedition of several archeomagical sites and obscure [[Legend]]s to find the truth that would give [[Humanity]] an edge over the tyranny of [[Pure Light]]. On his search he finds the obscure work of [[Vals Jenner]], the first epidemiologist that was studying the remnants of the [[Great Plague]], and uses this knowledge to become the first means of developing his own techniques. He uses the knowledge on the vaccines that [[Vals Jenner]] developed while searching for further clues on how to even conduct surgery. This is his formal foundation in medicine albeit self-taught, he further polishes his knowledge by pursuing other [[Legend]]s during his expeditions.

His search eventually makes him come to the [[Legend]] of the Killer of the Great Expanse. He begins searching for the truth of this [[Legend]], and after much dedication he finally uncovers the "treasure trove of sculptures" of the killer which have detailed logs and compositions of [[Spellweaving]] designed to create the tools necessary. The Beautifier also has detailed logs on the anatomy of body parts and some of the sculptures feature [[Pure Light]] beings, this is where [[Cadmus Tacet]] comes to the knowledge of both human organs and [[Coherence Binding Tissue]]. He later adopts his own style based on the teachings of [[Syvanth]]. He develops a vision too of _"There's even something to learn from monsters"_ to begin the dissection, study, and cruel experiments on [[Pure Light]] beings.

### Character Details

- He has a PTSD fear from his infancy of the clicking sound some of the dragons made before choosing a target for execution. This sound makes him instantly leave any areas during his expeditions, making him on the run as a permanent traveler of knowledge while knowing his own life is on the very line.
- When he eventually grows up, this ticking sound has still PTSD in him, he realizes by having his first "screw up" during vivisection precisely because of this noise that startled him while undergoing surgery as the patient's own throat bloated with blood. This is the visceral connection that reminds him that despite everything, he is still human.
- Despite being very violent towards [[Pure Light]] beings, he's actually fond of most humanoids that share similar structure preaching that they can actually coexist with humans, this includes a good amount of elves, human hybrids, demi humans that only have small differences such as fox ears or a tail. His "hard" limit for empathy is anything below 65% [[Auric Structure]].
- He's very gentle with human children and actually has a following around him by being a tutor in the arts of magic and primitive medicine. He actively teaches humans near him on how to do spells for healing and prevention of wounds worsening in both magical (without [[Strand]] magic) and non magical ways. He prioritizes non [[Spellweaver]]s as he sees that they are the most vulnerable.
- He is very devout follower of the [[Auric Order]], actively patronizing and sponsoring the pursuit of knowledge from both [[Humanity]] and the divine. He never misses any of the sermons and debates profoundly against [[Outer God]]s, the dependency on the esoteric and the [[Chorus Pillar]]. He actively lectures children as well on the tenets of the theological virtues and the importance of communion.
- On his [[Motif Awakening]] he received his cherished [[Auric Bell Staff]] from a mentor who took the risk of giving him the staff to attune for himself at 16. This was a transgression his mentor took because it usually requires being [[Lunar Cycle]] 20 of age to receive one. However, this was the first and most important comfort that he would receive his entire life. The hum of the chorus of everyone came before him were the bedrock for his psychological grounding for the [[Age of Humanity]] as he didn't even know his own parents. This "being on the shoulder of giants" to establish [[Mastery Over Chaos]] was his grounding principle on every hard choice. The time he almost lost the [[Auric Bell Staff]] he almost went insane looking for it as it was his entire support mechanism, which prompted him to establish a [[Soul-Binding]] ritual to keep it permanently with him to never lose it again.
- He loves animals that don't display magical properties, most commonly he prefers cattle and actively engages with [[Domestication Enclave]]s that aren't involved with [[Pure Light]] beings, sponsoring the development of human technology and coexisting with "safe" beings to the point of even pushing for animal rights. Furthermore, he has a deep respect for [[Agromagical Enclave]]s despite not sharing the same medicinal approach. He values them as the first "keepers of knowledge" due to the first uses of observation to create irrigation, culture and plantation techniques, he particularly praises the "domestication of magic" as means to enhance human survival.
- [[Auric Enclave]]s are his common ground during the early history of his exploration. Most of his knowledge comes from the mentorship of pious of the [[Auric Order]]. Although he never fully reveals his plans due to fear of retaliation and having a similar fate to that of [[Vals Jenner]]. Nonetheless, he relies actively on them as sources of information.

### Character Arc

**Arc 1: The Seed of Rage (Childhood Trauma and Exile)**

- [[Cadmus Tacet]] is born into one of the regions dominated by the [[Age of Horrors]] where draconic demi-human overlords subjugate humans as cattle.
- [[Cadmus Tacet]] is born from the result of one of the gruesome breeding rituals.
- [[Cadmus Tacet]] grows alongside humans cowering in the grass.
- [[Cadmus Tacet]] watches the execution of an unknown man by impaling his neck with a [[Crystal]] spear for not subjecting himself to one of the rituals.
- [[Cadmus Tacet]] burns the memory of the dying man into his memory. Before dying, the condemned man smiled a delivered a defiant prophecy "A day will come where [[Humanity]] will outlast their oppressors and the sons of his sons will use the very essence of these [[Pure Light]] beings as the fuel for the [[Age of Humanity]]."
- This was the seed of purpose that gave a young [[Cadmus Tacet]] hope in defiance.
- Before [[Cadmus Tacet]] reaches 13 years old, and he is forced to partake in the separation of new tributes, he manages to escape and is driven into exile, his terror was transmuted into a vow. He embarked on a desperate search to uncover the truth of what gave [[Pure Light]] beings their power and to survive.
- The seeds of his desperate escape cements his [[Legend Trait]] of [[Devoted]]. He will come to see this to the very end.
- Adopts his surname "Tacet" as that was the name of his homeland from which he had escaped.
- He represents the absolute bottom of the societal and magical hierarchy fighting back against the undisputed rulers of the world in memory of his home.

**Core**: Born into the cruelty of the [[Age of Horrors]] → Develops trauma and the seed of rage that will become the vow he dedicates his life to.
**Key Character Trait Formation**: Fear of subjugation becomes existential dread.
**Critical Purpose Seeded**: The quest of knowledge for the emancipation of [[Humanity]] from the chains of volatile magic.

**Arc 2: The Wandering Tutelage of the [[Auric Order]]**

- In his exile [[Cadmus Tacet]] seeks refuge in the nearest [[Auric Enclave]]. He pursues both safety, truth and knowledge from both himself and the divine.
- He learns the basic foundation of the [[Auric Order]], the concept of [[Perfect Reflection]], and the tenets of theological virtues.
- He even learns from the disasters that have preceded him, of both the [[Great Plague]] and of [[The Hollowing]]. He realizes that there's no answer in anything that isn't human. His education by wandering mentors and moving across [[Enclave]]s to escape the [[Age of Horrors]] is the start of his journey during the next four years.
- On his 16th birthday, after having moved thrice of location between [[Auric Enclave]]s, he tries desperately to understand why the heavens remain silent, and why is the underlying meaning of the world's cruelty. This pursue of the truth, of "Why is the world like this, what do [[Pure Light]] beings have have that we do not?" triggers his [[Motif Awakening]] to [[Luminance]], and in the depths of this crisis, he comes to understand that both his suffering and the [[Auric Aria]] gave him a divine mission: "To establish order into the chaos of [[Pure Light]]" just as the [[Auric Aria]] did when she wove pure chaos into structure when she built the [[Known Universe]] and [[Arcanoria]]. For him, this was the [[Perfect Reflection]].
- [[Cadmus Tacet]] becomes a fully fledged devout, and promises to mirror the achievements of his creator. His [[Ambitious]] [[Legend Trait]] evolves into [[Reality Bender]].
- He comes to the conclusion that while he appreciates the mentors that gave him a refuge for the remaining of his infancy, he has to pursue the truth on his own for anything truly revolutionary, he has to look at the records of those who were banished from society.
- [[Cadmus Tacet]] moves out of the [[Auric Enclave]] and into his quest for knowledge. He follows the lead of one scholar that was banished by the very [[Auric Order]], and starts his hunt for archeomagical sites and obscure [[Legend]]s.
- He starts his journey with nothing but a severe PTSD-induced fear of the clicking sounds the dragons made before executing someone.

- **The Search for Truth:** Seeking an edge over the tyranny of [[Pure Light]], [[Cadmus Tacet]] began his quest of knowledge across archeomagical sites and investigated obscure [[Legend]]s.
- **Psychological Shift**: From "Heavens are silent to injustice" to "The injustice of silence is the sacred mandate that I have to impose order" → messianic pragmatism.


**Arc 3: The Seed of Method (The Hunt for the Ghost of [[Vals Jenner]])**

- Driven by his newly evolved [[Reality Bender]] trait and his lead on the trail of an executed scholar, [[Cadmus Tacet]] scours archeomagical sites across the continent, looking for the very knowledge the [[Auric Order]] deemed too dangerous to keep.
- He comes to realize that the traces of the [[Great Plague]] are what drove this scholar to find a similar truth. He develops the mindset of _"I am not alone."_
- On several expeditions he hears the clicking of dragons which forces him to abandon his current location and continue with incomplete information but progressively unlocking more knowledge.
- He comes in contact with [[Indulgent Enclave]]s to create a party of someone that would manipulate [[Strand]] and allow him to uncover the further depths of [[Strand Pool]]s for following what would normally be "cold trials."
- After investigating several [[Memory Field]]s, he manages to triangulate the identity of [[Vals Jenner]]. This is the first grand case he has solved as a master detective.
- He uncovers the trove of suppressed and obscure research of Dr. [[Vals Jenner]], who he posthumously titled as [[Arcanoria]]'s first epidemiologist who studied the traces of the [[Great Plague]] and successfully developed a vaccine.
- From reading about her tragic fate, executed for treason and witchcraft by a superstitious society, [[Cadmus Tacet]] learns the foundations of rigorous observation, hypothesis, and self-taught medicine.
- More importantly, [[Vals Jenner]]’s death instills a dark psychological lesson: truth must be paired with power, and moral judgment is a function of power, not truth. To reveal a revolutionary truth prematurely is to invite destruction.
- He vows that his own work must be meticulously documented but kept entirely hidden from society until [[Humanity]] is ready to wield it. His [[Devoted]] [[Legend Trait]] evolves into [[Piercing Analyst]], allowing him to dissect both biology and human superstition without illusion and his newly honed skills in solving cold mysteries.

**Key Character Trait Formation**: Truth without power is suicide.
**Critical Purpose Seeded**: The quest of knowledge deepens as his own ability to solve cold trail cases hardens by his understanding of [[Memory Field]]s.

**Arc 4: The Seed of Technique (The [[Legend]] of the Twisted Beautifier)**

- [[Cadmus Tacet]]’s expeditions eventually lead him to the horrifying [[Legend]] of "The Twisted Beautifier" an unidentified medieval serial killer locally known as or "The Killer of the Great Expanse."
- This is the hardest case yet because he doesn't know if he's actually chasing a ghost, but the possibility of earning the knowledge of his allegedly [[Mastery Over Chaos]] killer techniques is a reward too high to pass by.
- He follows several leads across [[Memory Field]]s building incomplete knowledge but progressively getting closer to the truth.
- He passes several nights chasing a ghost and doubting the existence of the figure at all. Most leads leave him to cold or closed trials, and he reflects as the [[Legend]] truly seems like an elusive an elaborate fantasy of superstitions.
- During one of his expeditions, a nearby town is overrun by creatures of the [[Age of Horrors]]. He escapes a very near death solely because of his PTSD of the clicking sound. He anticipates before he's hunted himself and manages to survive by a very narrow margin.
- This experience makes him enter a despairing spiral but he grounds himself to the vow of making honor and justice to the surname he himself adopted. This is his motif awakening to [[Crystal]], and the dual-wielding of [[Ornament]]al magic allows him to finally key on the last piece of the puzzle. He uncovers an old name called [[Syvanth]].
- He follows this lead, and triangulates after much deliberate analysis of the possibilities of this assassin. The final breakthrough hits him after remembering the state of the [[Memory Field]] before he was nearly killed by the clicking of the dragon-kind. It happened that the PTSD clicking sound was rhythmic, and when paired in layers for the spells he barely survived plus his own panicking heartbeat it became a polyrhythm. The loud sound of his heart trying to escape his chest paired with the clicking sound were the key to cracking the code.
- He then mapped that exact same idea, of two overlapping frequencies, to the 21 cases he had been investigating. He realized [[Syvanth]] was operating on polyrhythms too and that his location wasn't erratic, it had a rhythm of a symphony he couldn't hear before. The eureka makes him understand that [[Syvanth]] was actually the legendary unknown killer.
- With this knowledge and determination, he manages to locate [[Syvanth]]'s jeweled location. When overlapping the rhythms of 1:3, 3:2, and 5:3 over the 21 cases, it mapped a giant star that pointed in the center to a location where [[Syvanth]] was. Following this lead, he found the hidden "treasure trove of sculptures," containing preserved, surgically disfigured bodies, incredibly detailed anatomical logs, and complex [[Spellweaving]] compositions for precision cutting.
- Opening the trove triggers a profound ethical crisis and epistemic vertigo. [[Cadmus Tacet]] is initially disgusted, recognizing the horrific cruelty of the serial killer.
- However, making a conscious choice to separate the monster's sadistic intent from his brilliant surgical technique, [[Cadmus Tacet]] adopts the philosophy that _"There's even something to learn from monsters."_ 
- This is the moment he accepts the weight of his own potential monstrosity for the sake of his mission. His [[Pragmatic]] [[Legend Trait]] evolves into [[Utilitarian Stoic]].
- He finally solved the impossible case of [[Syvanth]] the Twisted Beautifier and realizes he was using a combination of polyrhythms with elements and his own seductive whistling in an entrancing dance to dismember his victims while keeping them alive and suffering for as long as possible.
- He extracts [[Syvanth]]'s anatomical knowledge of human organs and his precise methods utilizing [[Crystal]], [[Cindergale]], and [[Luminance]] cutting jets. This grants [[Cadmus Tacet]] his first true understanding of the methodology of a surgeon.
- More importantly, alongside the sculptures of disfigured humans, [[Syvanth]] also experimented with [[Pure Light]] beings and established something he called as the "Dancing Organ," which for his twisted beauty was what made his sculptures fickle with light.
- The gruesome reports on this "Dancing Organ" were the final key that [[Cadmus Tacet]] required. He realized that magic came from this very organ, and that it was the holy grail of what he had been fighting to find so desperately. Later he coined the term [[Coherence Binding Tissue]] after [[Syvanth]]'s sculptures.
- Solving the impossible mystery of the polyrhythmic killer that no one could pinpoint before evolves his [[Piercing Analyst]] [[Legend Trait]] into his first [[Apex Trait]]: [[Clarity of Infinite Light]].


**[[Piercing Analyst]] milestone**: He uncovers the truth about the [[Legend]] of a serial killer who no one could catch. This is a massive victory for his intuition and is his first [[Apex Trait]]. He has both the Why, and the How to commence his vivisection.
**Testing of Ethical Boundaries**: The quest of knowledge makes him separate function from work. [[Syvanth]] was a ruthless monster but this delusion made him the best surgeon of all contemporary history albeit by an aesthetic sadism.

**Arc 5: The [[Legend]] of the Vivisector (The Age of Humanity)**

- Transmuting his childhood trauma into a frozen, surgical determination, [[Cadmus Tacet]] begins with capturing faes and [[Pure Light]] creatures.
- During his first vivisection, the visceral reality of his actions sets in. He experiences a severe "screw up" during the surgery precisely because the creature makes a clicking sound that triggers his PTSD from the draconic executioners of his youth. The panic reminds him that despite his cold exterior, he is still human.
- He establishes a strict, utilitarian boundary to protect his sanity: he sets a "hard limit" for empathy, feeling absolutely no compassion for anything possessing less than 65% [[Auric Structure]] (the threshold for [[Pure Light]] beings).
- Despite the gruesome cruelty he inflicts on magical creatures, a profound duality emerges in his character. He is exceptionally gentle with human children, actively tutoring vulnerable, non-[[Spellweaver]] humans in primitive medicine and healing.
- This newfound boundary is his [[Motif Awakening]] to [[Void]], and evolves his [[Utilitarian Stoic]] [[Legend Trait]] into the [[Apex Trait]] of [[Void-Embrace Anchor]]. He will accept all the necessary losses and will take the blame so long as he can continue to protect [[Humanity]], its heirs, and its children.
- He then becomes patron of some [[Enclave]]s such as [[Auric Enclave]]s for preaching his doctrine of [[Perfect Reflection]] and of [[Domestication Enclave]]s that handle non magical cattle.
- He holds deep respect for mundane animals and [[Agromagical Enclave]]s, praising their "domestication of magic" as the first true keepers of knowledge for human survival.
- In the quiet hours after his dissections, he meticulously records his findings in anatomical logs. This act of documentation is an act of hope, ensuring future generations will understand why he committed these atrocities.
- Looking at his accumulated knowledge and the possibility it represents to subdue the volatility of magic through human reason, [[Cadmus Tacet]] proudly coins his era the first true "[[Age of Humanity]]". His final [[Legend Trait]] of [[Reality Bender]] evolves into [[World Shaping Maverick]] after conducting the first crusade after the very [[Age of Horrors]] in his homeland.

**Arc 6: The Legacy of Iron (The Industrialization of Magic)**

- [[Cadmus Tacet]] eventually reaches the end of his mortal life, having completed his [[Magnum Opus]]: "The Scalpel of [[Humanity]]'s Hope". He ascends to the [[Stellar Legacy Score]] as a [[Constellation]], forever remembered as "The Vivisector" and "The Surgeon of Progress".
- Generations pass, and by [[Ages]] IX (the Industrial Era), [[Cadmus Tacet]]'s anatomical research and surgical methods are uncovered and scaled to a civilization level.
- Driven by the compounding historical trauma of apocalyptic plagues and predatory gods, [[Civilization]] enters the second "[[Age of Humanity]]".
- Applying [[Cadmus Tacet]]'s exact anatomical discoveries, humanity initiates the tragic [[Age of Sealing Iron]]. They build massive machines containing iron cages, systematically trapping faes and [[Pure Light]] beings inside.
- Humanity forces the innate magical essence of these trapped beings to act as mechanical engines, prioritizing absolute structural control over magic to guarantee absolute safety.
- The horrifying industrialization of [[Cadmus Tacet]]'s work flawlessly achieves the defiant prophecy of the Unknown Man from his childhood: [[Humanity]] outlasts their oppressors, using the boundless vitality of [[Pure Light]] gods as the mechanical fuel for human progress.
- In the future this boundary of the [[Pure Light]] spectrum is tested even further in the third [[Age of Humanity]] with the rise of division between "True Pure Blooded" [[Humanity]], and all other Demi Humans. Twisting the legacy of the peaceful coexistence that [[Cadmus Tacet]] himself provided for anything above 65%.

# Capital

The main city of any [[Civilization]].

# Cataclysmic Aftermath

#chaos #crisis #society 

The [[Cataclysmic Aftermath]]s, also known as the Great Filters are the three distinct [[Age Crisis]] of [[Gateway To Genesis]] that are unsolvable on the first try and plunge the world into a new timeline reset beginning from the [[Age of Desolation]]. Each of these is tied with [[The Ultimate Weapon]] and represents one essential part of the palindrome of the 3 x 4 x 7 that makes the amount of [[Beat]]s per [[Seventh]]. They are essential to the core loop of [[Arcanoria]] cyclical structure, are deeply tied with the progressive reveal of information about [[The Ultimate Weapon]], and the [[Crisis Wonders]].

The three [[Cataclysmic Aftermath]]s acting as Great Filters are the following [[Age Crisis]]:

- The [[Polychord Crisis]]: The first filter in [[Ages]] VI that is the culmination of the [[Holy War]] that ends with the master-key of [[The Ultimate Weapon]] being activated and the firing causes the end of the [[First Reset]] and [[Second Reset]].

- The MAD [[Wolf Bomb]] Annihilation: The second filter in [[Ages]] XI of the Atomic & Information [[Ages]] that culminates with the [[Institute]] of Anti Existence soteriology firing every single [[Wolf Bomb]] over all major population centers to reduce the world to ashes believing they are cutting the tail of the snake of the ouroboros of violence. However, their lack of knowledge about [[The Ultimate Weapon]] makes the attempt to end all existence futile.

- The Unraveling of [[Primal White Noise]]: The final filter in [[Ages]] XIII before the [[Age of The End]] which requires finishing the [[Sonata]] of Interwoven Threads of Gold and Silver (The [[Sonata]] of [[Arcanoria]]) to unlock the final escape by creating [[A True Sine Wave]] which represents the change from [[Civilization]] to the Third Actor representing the first time the game breaks the fourth wall to find a [[Consciousness]] without existence, recognizing that there is one type of [[Consciousness]] that wasn't born within [[The Eternal Symphony]] and is the key to the new Age of Genesis.

Each of them are a pivotal moment for [[Arcanoria]] and have each several implications on unlocking various layers of knowledge and of gameplay. The [[Divine Reset]] mechanic and the Prestige is tied to the [[Achievement]]s unlocked in total of all the runs.

The resets are the following:

- [[First Reset]]: The [[Old Testament]] era when the [[Auric Aria]] came back from her silence of the [[Lost Cycle]]. Before the Game.

- [[Second Reset]]: The doomed [[New Testament]] and beginning of the game which ends with the [[Polychord Crisis]]. Early Game.

- [[Third Reset]]: The first half of the real game, it is more than one reset depending on the player, but the entire part is named [[Third Reset]] until they clear both [[Sonata]]s of the [[Auric Aria]] and of [[Selenea]], concludes in the MAD Annihilation. Mid Game.

- [[Fourth Reset]]: The second half and final stage of the real game, it is likewise too more than one reset depending on how many [[Divine Reset]]s [[Civilization]] incurs but it is the last stage of the game until the very [[Age of The End]]. Late Game.

The Master-Key evolves in 4 phases:

- Tier 1: Acquired after [[Civilization]] fails the doomed [[Second Reset]] [[Polychord Crisis]] and the [[Auric Aria]] uses the last tether between them to reveal [[The Truth of Arcanoria]]. This is the transition from the Early Game to the Early Mid Game.

- Tier 2: Acquired after [[Civilization]] in the [[Third Reset]] successfully navigates and acquires the Master-Key proper breaking the loop of the [[Polychord Crisis]]. Transition from the Early Mid Game to the entire Mid Game.

- Tier 3: Acquired after [[Civilization]] fails the [[Wolf Bomb]] Annihilation during the Third World War in [[Ages]] XI. This unlocks the counter of [[The Ultimate Weapon]], reveals advanced [[Crisis Wonders]] and transitions into the Early Late Game.

- Tier 4: Acquired after [[Civilization]] finishes the [[Sonata]] of [[Arcanoria]]. This signals the true Late Game and unlocks the [[Age of The End]].

### The [[Polychord Crisis]]

This crisis attempts to make the 3 of the equation reduced to 0 by attacking the [[Trinity Harmony]] and its continuity to unravel reality. 0 x 4 x 7

This major [[Age Crisis]] unlocks two layers of gameplay:

- It signals the end of the [[Second Reset]] through [[The Truth of Arcanoria]] that unlocks many layers, secrets, the presence of [[Crisis Wonders]], and begins the [[Sonata]] of the Golden Sovereign and the [[Sonata]] of the Pale [[Moon]]. This is the access through the truth to the Tier 1 Outside of [[The Ultimate Weapon]] which is what makes [[Civilization]] claim the Master-Key.

- It formally begins the "[[Third Reset]]" which allows fulfilling and passing the filter of the [[Polychord Crisis]], unlocking this awards [[The Ultimate Weapon]] Master-key which gives [[Civilization]] the ability to use the [[Divine Reset]] mechanic, enhancing the future runs of the [[Third Reset]].

- Successfully navigating in the [[Third Reset]] the [[Polychord Crisis]] unlocks [[Ages]] VIII, IX, X, and XI. until the second Great Filter of the MAD [[Wolf Bomb]] Annihilation. It also unlocks [[Crisis Wonders]] but without the ability to purify them into proper [[Megastructure Wonder]]s. Surviving the [[Polychord Crisis]] starts counting time before and after the crisis, and the Master-Key reacts unlocking the Tier 2 Outer Layer and unlocking the first layer of the wish: _"I wish for [ < s̵i̶g̷n̸a̷l̶ ̴l̷o̸s̷t̷ > ... ] fate... to reverse [ ... c̷o̶r̵r̷u̷p̷t̷e̵d̵ ... ]... before [[Civilization]] even began... to [ ... b̵l̵a̸n̸k̵ ... ]... the [[Ages]] [ ... < v̷o̶i̵c̷e̵ ̴f̷r̸a̷c̷t̷u̶r̵e̷s̵ > ... ]... if the [ N O I S E ]... ever destroys [ ... r̸e̵-̶f̸r̸a̷g̵m̴e̴n̵t̵s̷ ... ]... No matter how [ ... h̷e̴a̷v̶y̶ ̶s̵t̵a̴t̸i̴c̶ ... ] lives it takes...  [D I R E C T I V E]..."_

This begins the [[Sonata]] of the Golden Sovereign and the [[Sonata]] of the Pale [[Moon]].
[[Hypermage]]
### The MAD [[Wolf Bomb]] Annihilation

_"The selfish intent of trying to preserve peace initiates wars, genocides and justifiable atrocities in the name of shameless justice."_ [[Wolf Tone]] [[Institute]]

This crisis attempts to make the 7 of the equation reduced to 0 by attacking the [[Auric Heptacode]] and its topology to unravel reality. 3 x 4 x 0

This is the second [[Age Crisis]] and Great Filter that separates the previous [[Ages]] which is triggered by the accelerationist anti existence [[Institute]] league of the [[Wolf Tone]]. It is the climax of the Third World War of [[Arcanoria]]. It is the division between the old world fantasy and the sci-fi aspect of [[Gateway To Genesis]].

- The hyper accelerationist [[Institute]] of [[Ages]] XI, [[Wolf Bomb]]  Anti Existence. onwards believes in soteriology by the death of the [[Known Universe]]: "One day we will all return to the static that precedes the very existence of the cosmos." Their rush to end the world is a driver to the next MAD reset. "The stars fall from the sky, the world is reborn." The [[Institute]] preaches that [[Primal White Noise]] is the true god of the universe and that it's impossible to break the ouroboros cycle of violence as wars have existed from the very beginning of [[Humanity]] and will continue to exist long after these [[Ages]] so the best thing they can do is to cut the tail of the snake and eradicate all life. Their logo is a nuclear symbol alongside the depiction of a wolf. 

- The catastrophe is triggered after the previous Two World Wars have already occurred and it is the climax resolution of the [[Wolf Tone]] [[Institute]] after they manage to denotate every [[Wolf Bomb]] levelling all of [[Arcanoria]]. Once they win they will declare in the cinematic, as the [[Wolf Bomb]] detonations blast the skies and the earth they preach, "It's finally over. The [[Cycle]] is broken. No more Death, no more Revolutions, no more Wars. No tyrant will become the head of the snake ever again." This formally begins the "[[Fourth Reset]]."

- [[The Ultimate Weapon]], however, salvages the doomed timeline and unlocks its Tier 3 Inner Layer within the Master-Key. This unlocks advanced [[Crisis Wonders]] which include the ruined cities of [[Civilization]] that were nuked by the [[Wolf Bomb]]s. Instead of being isolated complex, the advanced [[Crisis Wonders]] are incredibly advanced arrays of [[Megastructure Wonder]]s, ranging from planetary disks, to factories, to ruined space elevators, and several types of weaponry and skyscrapers. It also makes every previous [[Crisis Wonders]] able to be enhanced into [[Megastructure Wonder]]s giving them back their former glory.

- Tier 3 Inner Layer also unlocks some [[Scorching Truth]]s about [[The Ultimate Weapon]]. It reveals the amount of [[Cycle]]s it has been counting since its inception, the count of the total [[Cycle]]s in [[Arcanoria]] will be the amount of [[Cycle]]s of the [[Third Reset]], the [[Second Reset]], and the [[First Reset]], plus any number generated on the very start of the game which is between 100,000 and 10,000,000 [[Cycle]]s, signaling the impossible length of the [[Lost Cycle]]. This number will induce vertigo for most players once they come to realize the truth, and that the [[Lost Cycle]] wasn't just a dark [[Ages]] primitive period, it reached Sci-Fi levels even further than [[Ages]] XI. # Civic

_"If the [[Pillars]] of [[Civilization]] are what builds its tenets, [[Civic]] are what makes them real through practices, tradition, culture, and everyday life. A [[Civilization]] is the song it chooses to sing."_

These are the unit blocks that form the identity and [[Resonance]] of any [[Civilization]]. It encodes activities, laws, culture, rituals, and practices that codify and integrate the [[Arcanoria]]'s deep magical laws with the governance of its empires. Thus [[Civic]]s are very versatile and evolve to reflect the progression of [[Humanity]] through the [[Ages]] and their evolving relationship with magic, crisis, and power.

[[Civic]] occupy too the spectrum of [[Consonance]] and [[Dissonance]], which can range between idyllic democratic practices to horrific military tactics. They are divided into the same categories as [[Enclave]]s:

- Agromagical [[Civic]]: Growth, Health, Sanitation, Sustenance.
- Militant [[Civic]]: Tactics, Weapons, Mercenaries, Hunters.
- Auric [[Civic]]: [[Aureus Pillar]], [[Piety]], [[Faith]], Knowledge, Science.
- Weaver [[Civic]]: [[Waltz Pillar]], Culture, Poetry, Songs, Communal Arts.
- Domestication [[Civic]]: Creatures, [[Pure Light]], Taming, Druids.
- Trading [[Civic]]: Economics, Wealth, [[Resources]], Efficiency. 
- Industrious [[Civic]]: Equipment, Forges, Artisans, Metalworks.
- Regal [[Civic]]: [[Regalia Pillar]], Politics, Diplomacy, Prestige, Espionage.
- Indulgent [[Civic]]: Entertainment, Pleasure, Joy, Luxuries,
- Esoteric [[Civic]]: [[Chorus Pillar]], [[Outer God]]s, Dark [[Magic Arts]], Witchcraft, Spirits.

### Tier 1 [[Ages]] [[Civic]]s ([[Ages]] 0 - III)

#### Agromagical, Indulgent, Weaver & Domestication [[Civic]]s

**Culinary Alchemists | Agromagical [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I-III | [[Consonance]]**

Practical magical cooking using locally harvested ingredients to create temporary spell enhancements. All the recipes are shared communally, and each village maintains a Flavor Log recording which ingredient combinations produce stable [[Resonance]]. Chefs are considered essential laborers.

[[Ballad]]s:
- In a starving settlement, an untalented chef finds an ancient recipe capable of stabilizing the entire village's psychological [[Composure]]. Because the required rare ingredient is deep within a deadly [[Vibrational Fallout]] zone, the chef must convince a traumatized, half-broken [[Spellweaver]] to escort them, turning foraging into a desperate fight for survival.

**Feast of Abundance | Indulgent [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I-III | [[Consonance]]**

Surplus goods and [[Auric Peach]]es are thrown from towers into public squares in a mandatory act of redistribution. Wealth held past the festival date is taxed as hoarding. [[Legend]]s in power who give the most during the feast earn higher social legitimacy, and some communities maintain records of each feast's yields and distribution, and farmers are honored as [[Civic]] [[Pillars]] equal to [[Spellweaver]]s.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A manipulative aristocrat attempts a bloodless coup by hiding vast wealth in magical [[Void]]-pockets to evade the hoarding tax, planning a massive distribution to instantly buy the public's loyalty. An undercover Justiciar must expose this economic sabotage before the feast crowns a tyrant.

**[[Ballad]] & Fantasy Plays | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] II–IV | [[Consonance]]**

The formal organization of writers, singers, poets, and composers into state-sanctioned guilds designed to create culture, new stories, and preserve the [[Ballad]]s of [[Legend]]s. The classical civilization of [[Iridia]] is noted as a major patron of this [[Civic]], officially sponsoring writers of fiction and fairytales to weave them into the empire's culture.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A state-sponsored playwright uncovers a "[[Scorching Truth]]"— on how the [[Civilization]]'s founding hero was actually a cowardly deserter that became an [[Atonalis]]. Knowing the [[Auric Order]] executes those holding forbidden knowledge, the playwright encodes the truth into a propagandist play, sparking a psychological thriller of censorship and treason under the king's nose in a play akin to Shakespeare's Hamlet.

**Ritual [[Whistling Fans]] Dancers | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] II–VI | [[Consonance]]**

Cultural and martial ceremonies inspired by [[Sephira]] (the [[Mythic Virtuoso]] of [[Cindergale]]), which utilize [[Whistling Fans]] as a formal patronage to the arts of [[Dance]] and martial combat.

[[Ballad]]s:
- During a grand martial ceremony, a young dancer realizes their rival's [[Whistling Fans]] are tuned to a [[Dissonance]] designed to shatter their internal [[Coherence]] and trigger a panic attack that interrupts the ceremony to crown them de jure heir. The dancer must instantly adapt their choreography to survive a deadly acoustic battle disguised as a synchronized duet.

**Moonlit Vigil | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0-III | [[Consonance]]**

Courtship rituals in [[Glimmerfern]] groves during a full [[Moon]]. In silence people meet a matching frequency. Practiced by [[Waltz Pillar]], [[Chorus Pillar]], peasants and refugees. It is a _The folk tradition of the broken world._ in the last pockets that dim with hope to create love. 

[[Ballad]]s:
- A noble [[Spellweaver]] sneaks into a peasant Vigil and falls deeply in love by phase-locking in perfect [[Sympathetic Vibration]] with a commoner [[Spellweaver]]. When their family demands a loveless political marriage, the couple must choose whether to sever their true magical connection or ignite a civil war.

**The Ball Fluff Runs | Domestication [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I-VI | [[Consonance]]**

Periodic runs through city streets pursued by specially bred [[Pure Light]] creatures that are giant fluff sticky balls, whomever reaches the finish line without being touched by one gets to win the produce of these domesticated creatures.

**Horned Flag Stampedes | Domestication [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] II-VI | [[Cusp]]

Runs inspired by the Ball Fluff Runs but using bull-like [[Pure Light]] creatures which have [[Crystal]]-tipped horns. During these runs, regular people can get injured, and there are several flags left in the arena, the survivors who earn the most flags while still standing in the arena of the bulls gets to have a feast with the cooked [[Pure Light]] creatures afterward.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A disgraced knight enters the deadly Horned Flag Stampede to win a feast for starving orphans. A conspirator in the crowd casts a polyphonic spell to frenzy the beasts, turning the game into a massacre. The knight drops their weapons, using only wits and evasion to protect the other runners.

#### Auric, Trading & Industrious [[Civic]]s

[[Demi-Human]] Slave Trade [[Dissonance]]

indentured Servitude [[Dissonance]]

#### Regal, Militant & Esoteric [[Civic]]s

**Truth [[Soul Leitmotif]] Testimonies | Regal [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I Onwards | [[Consonance]]

A legal and social practice that requires individuals to use the dormant state of their [[Soul Leitmotif]] when signing social contracts. Because the [[Soul Leitmotif]] is a physical crystallization of one's [[Consciousness]] and emotional truth, this [[Civic]] effectively uses the bare soul as a flawless lie detector to build social harmony and trust.

[[Ballad]]s:
- An infamous spy infiltrates a rival empire to sign a doomed peace treaty, using [[Illusory Magic]] to project a false aura of Pristine [[Composure]] over their corrupted soul while framing the legitimate ruler of lying by flickering conflict to their [[Soul Leitmotif]]. A low-ranking clerk spots a microscopic flicker of [[Dissonance]] and must prove the deception before war erupts.

**Harmonic Quorum | Regal [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] I-III | [[Consonance]]**

Major policy decisions require a [[Resonance]] as majority vote. The assembled leadership must attuned their internal [[Coherence]] and [[Soul Leitmotif]]s onto a single frequency. If the leaders cannot achieve [[Sympathetic Vibration]] due to doubt or conflict, the policy cannot pass.

[[Ballad]]s:
- The council has one hour to pass a defensive edict against an encroaching demon swarm, but the Quorum fails because one hidden member is secretly terrified and generating [[Discordant Interference]]. The protagonist must interrogate the council's minds to find the coward before the walls are breached.

**Bridal Conquest | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0–III | [[Cusp]]**

A political and martial practice involving the capture of enemy rulers or high-ranking knights of the opposite sex to marry them into their [[Civilization]]. This [[Civic]] provides a the Bridal casus belli. Allowing [[Civilization]] to capture opposing enemies and instead of executing them, the ritual of courtship is meant to systematically create and secure strong lineages of magical heirs that unify cultures.

[[Ballad]]s:
- An undefeated warlord is forced into marriage with the empress who decimated their homeland. Over years, they develop genuine love. Just as they admit their [[Resonance]], the warlord's former generals breach the capital to assassinate the empress, forcing the warlord to turn against their own people to protect their captor.

**Hunting Parties of [[Legend]]s | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] II–IV | [[Consonance]]**

Coordinated hunting parties of great renown of top [[Spellweaver]]s in groups of 4 to 7, each assigned a specific role, to track and kill high-ranking [[Atonalis]] and [[Pure Light]] Behemoths. Successful hunts forge permanent synergy bonds, prestige, and yield pristine rare materials, pelts, and [[Rose Seed]]s.

[[Ballad]]s:
- Tracking an [[Ascendant]] [[Atonalis]] into a collapsed pass, a hunting party realizes the monster is perfectly anticipating them because it is the shattered [[Soul Leitmotif]] of their original mentor. Their fallen mentor uses the shared memories to turn the hunters against one another, and exploit their individual weaknesses.

**Duels of Severance | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0-III | [[Cusp]]**

When a child reaches the age of majority, they are required to duel their most direct guardian in a brutal, near‑death contest that ends only when one combatant is permanently marked. The wound is proof the duel is fought for honor, witnessed by the community, and won only when one opponent inflicts a decisive injury on the other. Killing is neither required nor forbidden, but the duel only ends through the submission of one of the fighters due to physical exhaustion. The ritual is proof that the chord of dependency has been severed so that both may now relate as equals.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A gifted [[Spellweaver]] must duel their chronically ill father. Inflicting a permanent wound might kill him, but refusing leaves them legally classified as a child, unable to inherit the magical legacy needed to save their estate. The duel becomes a heart-wrenching dance of pulled punches.

**[[Leylines]] Nomads | Esoteric [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0-III | [[Consonance]]**

Societies that move with the [[Grand Thread Rings]] instead of installing [[Resonance Anchors]] whenever [[Leylines]] move during [[Age Transition]]s, they follow the natural flow of [[Cosmic Motion]] to determine where to establish themselves. Similar to Air Nomads in Avatar.

**[[Sky Glass]] Burials | Esoteric [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0–III | [[Consonance]]**

Funerary and cultural ceremonies involving "sky burying" at the edges of high mountain peaks where [[Sky Glass]] forms naturally. These ceremonies are deeply connected to the tactile, infinite fractals of the glass, and are a reverence to the skies for allowing a sacred passage into the [[Auroral Ribbons]] and [[The Eternal Symphony]].

[[Ballad]]s:
- During a sacred [[Sky Glass]] Burial, the elder is terrified of death and begins spiraling into an [[Atonalis]] to at least have immortality in this state, before he can die the elder hatches into a violent [[Violux]] [[Atonalis]]. The unarmed mourners must use the howling wind and raw [[Resonance]] to push the demon off the cliff without destroying the sacred grounds.

**Chaos Reverence Sacrifices | Esoteric [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] 0-II | [[Dissonance]]**

Rituals of communal suicide and sacrifice to reverence the chaotic energy that emerges, these societies sacrifice and create suffering to pool [[Formless Masses]] that become revered as "divinity" when they emerge from a [[Dissonance]] Cocoon. This is one of the earliest ways to realize [[We Are Atonalis]], because the emerging [[Atonalis]] is what is being revered as a chaotic entity as divinity due to its anomalous properties made from the collective suffering these societies are ignorant to.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A runaway infiltrates a death cult about to pool enough trauma to birth a [[Fracted]] [[Atonalis]]. Armed only with a [[Resonance Box]], they must disrupt the chanting with a perfectly timed counter-frequency and crash the entire sacrifice ritual before the demon is allowed to hatch from the collective suffering.

### Tier 2 [[Ages]] [[Civic]]s ([[Ages]] IV - VI) ([[Law of Relics]] Established)

#### Agromagical, Indulgent, Weaver & Domestication [[Civic]]s

**Cooking Guilds** Evolution of Culinary Alchemists

[[Ballad]]s:
- The grandmaster of a prestigious guild discovers a rival is lacing bread with [[EC]] (Euphoria Compound) as remnants from the [[Great Plague]] to slowly hijack the city guards' nervous systems. Discredited, the grandmaster wages an underground culinary war by creating purifying, anti-toxin meals with the knowledge of [[Vals Jenner]] to break the addiction before a coup occurs.

**Carnival of Shifting Reflections | Indulgent [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VI | [[Cusp]]**

Temporary magical costumes projected by [[Magical Relic]]s that allow participants to become someone else with shapeshifting [[Illusory Magic]]. Any citizen may wear the costume of a ruler, legend, or mythological figure during the [[Ritual Seventh]] of any [[Phase]]. Be it peasant as knight, widow as lost husband. The festival inverts social hierarchy for three days, releasing pressure through playful transformation.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A downtrodden tailor uses an illusion to assume the shape of the city’s ruthless [[Head of State]] to enjoy absolute luxury. The carnival of illusion turns lethal when elite assassins strike thinking he is the real king. Unable to drop the illusion without being executed by the state for treason, the tailor must outwit the killers while maintaining the cruel tyrant persona.

**Polyphonic Choral Singers | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VI | [[Consonance]]**

An institution of organized state-managed choral singers of multiple overlayed voices using bells and other [[Magical Relic]]s to enhance the [[Coherence]] of regions. These choruses are versatile and can be used for a variety of applications from agromagical applications to recovery and rebuilding of societies.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A soprano in the royal choir realizes the state is using their complex sheet music to weave a massive Signal Override, erasing the fundamental frequencies of political dissidents. The singer must recruit choristers to secretly weave a counter-melody to shatter the mind-control without breaking harmony.

**Courting Grounds | Weaver [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV | [[Consonance]]**

Evolution of Moonlit Vigil where once per spring, [[Phase of Prelude]], unwed citizens process in a botanical sanctuary beneath the palace gardens. [[Spellweaver]]s in this tradition use their [[Soul Leitmotif]]s to pulse in unison as means to find a partner and conduct rituals of romance and falling in love. Hook: Two rival noble houses both send heirs to the Courts. The heirs resonate—but their families are locked in a blood feud. Romeo & Juliet [[Ballad]].

[[Ballad]]s:
- The heirs of two noble houses locked in a centuries-old blood feud pulse in absolute, flawless unison at the Courting Grounds. State law mandates they marry, forcing the two families into a deadly, covert race to assassinate the opposing heir before the wedding binds their houses. Romeo & Juliet.

**Underground Pleasure Colosseums | Indulgent [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV |  [[Dissonance]]**

Jerez Arena as an evolution of the colosseum [[Civic]]s but focused on slaves gaining freedom but with painful and humiliating dehumanizing punishments on loss. Some of the contracts are directly paired with [[Velvet Nectar]].

#### Auric, Trading & Industrious [[Civic]]s

**Memory Markets | Trading [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV–VII | [[Dissonance]]**

Designated economic zones and sites where [[Velvet Nectar]] and its derivations are kept on a zone of exempted legal status and actively traded.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A desperate smuggler steals a vial of [[Velvet Nectar]] to pay a debt, unknowingly consuming the extracted memories of a renowned [[Great Spellweaver]]. Now possessing the dead mage's magical mastery, they are hunted by aristocratic connoisseurs who want the memories back.

**Slave & Servitude Auctions | Trading [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VII | [[Dissonance]]**
Underground trafficking rings with slaves of any species, whether used as commodity, servitude, or livestock.

**[[Contract Arts]] Slavery Guilds [[Dissonance]]**
Using contracts on [[Pure Light]] beings and [[Demi-Human]]s with high enough affinity to be subdued through slave marks as a combination between [[Mind Control Arts]] and [[Contract Arts]] as a perversion of [[Sympathetic Magic]].

#### Regal, Militant & Esoteric [[Civic]]s

**Trafficking Rings Conquests | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VII | [[Dissonance]]**
Slavery through subjugated regions that fell due to a slaver causus belly

**Species Caste System | Regal [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VII [[Dissonance]]**
Dividing citizens by tiers of classification depending on their [[Pure Light]] and [[Auric Structure]] between each races of [[Humanity]] and [[Demi-Human]]s.

**Legendary Hunting Charters | Regal [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV-VII | [[Consonance]]**

When a great beast or [[Atonalis]] threatens a region, the [[Head of State]] issues an open Hunt Charter, a state-sponsored named hunt available to any [[Legend]]. The kill is distributed a hunters council who weigh each participant's contribution, courage, and narrative role. Every charter is inscribed as a civic record, building a living history of who the [[Civilization]] chooses to honor.

[[Ballad]]s:
- An aging, dishonored [[Legend]] takes a near-suicidal hunt to clear their name, only to be ambushed by an arrogant aristocrat trying to steal the kill. When the [[Carnalix]] [[Atonalis]] traps them both in a collapsed ravine built from flesh, the rivals must work together to survive, and vanquish the [[Ascendant]] demon.

**Slayer's Amphitheater | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV–VI | [[Cusp]]**

Public arenas where volunteers, and sometimes prisoners, fight captured [[Atonalis]] before a crowd. Spectators' emotional resonance amplifies the slayer's magic, turning combat into a ritual of communal courage and monster research.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A political [[Spellweaver]] prisoner thrown into the arena against an impossible demon realizes they can manipulate the crowd's roaring emotions. Turning the cheers into a wave of [[Flux]] magic, the prisoner harnesses the collective [[Resonance]] to shatter their magical restraints and incite a bloody rebellion.

**[[Atonalis]] Bombs | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] V Onwards | [[Dissonance]]**

A brutal military tactic inspired by [[Institute]]s where a [[Civilization]] deliberately captures or tortures guilty [[Spellweaver]]s with the explicit intent of forcing their [[Consciousness]] to fracture and collapse into an [[Atonalis]]. These individuals are then sent to infiltrate a rival society as a Trojan horse, inevitably transforming into a destructive demon from inside the walls of an enemy [[Major Settlement]] to cause mass chaos.

[[Ballad]]s:
- A [[Spellweaver]] is tortured into an [[Atonalis]] Bomb and dumped in their own hometown. Feeling their soul cracking and mere hours from hatching into a monster, they must use failing willpower to run as far away from their loved ones as possible, racing to find a wasteland where they can die safely.

**Spiraling Conscription | Militant [[Civic]] | [[Ages]] IV Onwards | [[Dissonance]]**

Inspired by [[Institute]]s, [[Civilization]] utilizes [[Spellweaver]]s who have critically low [[Composure]] as state-sanctioned expedition units. These already half-broken individuals are deliberately deployed into highly hazardous areas, such as [[Vibrational Fallout]] zones and the outer territories of wild magic, gambling on whether the [[Spellweaver]] will break toward an [[Atonalis]] demon or push through the trauma. _"They are already half-broken. The question is whether they break toward the [[Atonalis]] or through it."_

[[Ballad]]s:
- A squad of four highly traumatized conscripts are dropped into wild magic. Instead of breaking, they form an intense level of [[Echoing Bonds]], triggering secondary [[Motif Awakening]]s that make them powerful enough to return to the capital and overthrow the generals who sent them to die.

### Tier 3 [[Ages]] [[Civic]]s ([[Ages]] VII-X)

**Bloodline Tithe | [[Ages]] VII–IX | [[Cusp]]**

Primarily used during the [[Age of Blood]], this [[Civic]] is a systemic tax where noble families must pay the state in blood. The eldest child of a noble house must undergo the Bloodline Tithe, during which a portion of their blood is stored in a family "Hemovault". This accumulated [[Essence Sacrifice]] acts as a familial military battery, drawn upon during wartime to fuel massive [[Civilization]] spells.

- [[Ballad]]s: The eldest daughter of a disgraced noble house goes to offer her blood, only to discover the Hemovault is completely empty. A corrupt government faction has secretly siphoned the generations of [[Essence Sacrifice]] to power an illegal apocalyptic superweapon. Branded a traitor, she must ally with underground [[Void]]-weavers to destroy the weapon before the government drains the life force of every noble family sacrifice made in the empire.

### Tier 4 [[Ages]] [[Civic]]s ([[Ages]] XI-XIV)

**Enhanced Magical Girl Polyphony | [[Ages]] XI | [[Consonance]]**

Inspired by the polyphonic practices of earlier [[Ages]] this ensemble is unique to the [[Age of Starlight]] using the principle of [[Echoing Bonds]] to establish strong [[Resonance Anchors]] within its cast of [[Spellweaver]]s through [[Harmonic Entanglement]].

The recipe promises a meal that can perfectly stabilize the psychological Composure of the entire village, but it requires a rare ingredient found only deep within a Vibrational Fallout zone. - **The Narrative Hook:** A manipulative aristocrat plots to seize the title of Head of State without shedding a single drop of blood. By secretly hoarding vast amounts of wealth in hidden Void-pockets to avoid the hoarding tax, they plan a massive, unprecedented distribution at the Feast of Abundance to instantly buy the absolute loyalty of the populace. The dancer must adapt their choreography on the fly, fighting a deadly acoustic battle disguised as a beautiful, synchronized duet.

# Civilization

The player, also referred to as the Third Actor

# Click Power

#mechanic #society 

[[Click Power]] is a core mechanic of [[Gateway To Genesis]], as the game begins as an incremental strategy clicker, the main UI allows for creating either [[Vital Resources]], aligned with vitality and [[Lunehymn]] or [[Building Materials]] which are aligned with creation, structure and [[Aetherlight]], mirroring the [[Dual Confluence Stream]].

Traditionally, [[Click Power]] behaves at the beginning of the game like a production button to generate [[Resources]]. However, upon acquiring the first [[Ceremonial Arts]] and [[Magic Arts]] of [[Civilization]], [[Gateway To Genesis]] swaps from mindlessly clicking into a rhythm based minigame mirroring Taiko No Tatsujin where playing a [[Spellweaving]] song of their [[Symphony Card]]s allows for a much higher yield of [[Resources]] and [[Morale]] boosts as celebration.

The Taiko No Tatsujin aspect is divided into pressing either Auric Symbols, representing [[Aetherlight]], the [[Auric Aria]] or Silvery Symbols representing the [[Moon]], and [[Lunehymn]]. By pressing each of these in rhythm in Perfect, [[Civilization]] unlocks the bar of [[Perfect Focus]] and Flow State that increases the total yield of [[Resources]] given by the rhymical ritual of their [[Civilization]].

This mechanic actively prevents auto clickers from being fully functional in [[Gateway To Genesis]], while adding an upgraded layer of rhythm, performance, and strategy to it. It ties directly to [[Click Power]]. Purely clicking by the sake of clicking generates [[Discordant Interference]].

# Coherence

How likely something is to exist, it is the contrary of chaos and [[Primal White Noise]]. Giving [[Coherence]] to the [[Known Universe]] is the primary objective of both the [[Auric Heptacode]] and the [[Trinity Harmony]]. It's a fundamental part of [[Spellweaving]] as well as it is the basis of [[Absolute Certainty]].

High [[Coherence]] forms [[Stable Harmonic Channels]] for information and magical transit through the [[Great Harmonic Loom]].

[[Coherence]] is not the absence of chaos, but rather a pattern so profound it can maintain integrity even at the edge of total dissolution.

# Combat System

#mechanic #society #spellweaving 

_Strategy is Composition. Combat is Performance._

The Symphony of War is the [[Combat System]] of [[Arcanoria]] that is divided into two core axioms. The macro layer determines what tools exist in the battle. The micro layer determines how well those tools are realized:

- **Macro Level | Strategy as Composition:** Wars are won before a single note is played. It consists of the system of building and preparing [[Orchestral Formation]]s, Assigning [[Legend]] [[Battle Conductor]]s, and [[Magic Arts]] made by [[Civilization]] alongside the technologies researched and invented as equipment, gear, and tier of [[Production Units]].

- **Micro Level | Combat as Performance:** The attacks are dictated by [[Symphony Card]]s which consist of actions such as combat attacks with traditional swords, [[Magic Arts]] for imbuing offensive, defensive, and utility magic. All combats are driven by army compositions named [[Orchestral Formation]]s which determine in the hex combat grid the positions of Units. This part features a rhythm based layer of repeating the melody back to increase the attack power of the [[Chord Layering]] Stack, and in the defense is playing the opposite melody in rhythm as noise cancellation.

Every mechanical decision flows from this philosophy. At the strategic layer,  [[Civilization]], as the architect of war a drafting armies, growing [[Legend]]s, preparing the score by composing from the slots of unlocked [[Magic Arts]] by discovering [[The Registers of Magic]], and advancing through the technology tree and developing cultural [[Civic]]s. 

However, at the tactical layer, they are a performer of their songs in the battlefield, moving from flawless execution of rhythm, [[Spellweaving]] [[Chord Layering]], and inverse-frequency defense that determines whether the score becomes a masterpiece or a catastrophe.

The system is designed to merge grand-strategy war planning, the long term development of civ-like 4X through magical development of [[Magic Arts]], understanding of [[Spellweaving]], and the customization of a roguelike deck builder through [[Symphony Card]]s  as an expression of [[Civic]]s and [[Legend]]s with a high-intensity tactical combat loop on the tempo of a rhythm game.

# Composure

#mechanic #spellweaving 

The level of stress, sanity, and meter of the internal [[Coherence]] of any [[Spellweaver]].

To lose [[Composure]] is to lose oneself, if all [[Composure]] is lost at the level of surrender, the [[Soul Leitmotif]] fractures, enveloping the [[Spellweaver]] in pure [[Dissonance]]. 

When the cocoon hatches in a wave of [[Discordant Interference]], what walks out is an [[Atonalis]], no longer a person nor [[Spellweaver]] but a broken hungry husk permanently trapped in the torturing paradox of an existence without [[Coherence]].

Thus, [[Composure]] is the most important metric for any [[Spellweaver]], it is visible in the [[Soul Leitmotif]] as it gets cloudy with muddy black [[Dissonance]] that becomes blacker and cloudier the closer a [[Spellweaver]] is to surrender and [[Corruption]].

[[Composure]] consists of 5 stress levels on the [[Soul Leitmotif]] that mirror that of the growth phases of an [[Atonalis]] from [[Nascent]] to [[Primal Discordia]]:

- Pristine: The perfect rest state for a [[Soul Leitmotif]], it is vibrant in color, beautiful, and emits light with the color of its primary binding. Usually represents a peaceful and [[Consonance]] filled state of mind. Momentarily, a [[Soul Leitmotif]] can become pristine on intense moments of joy.

- Clouded: This is the normal state for most [[Spellweaver]]s, it has the vibrant light of the primary binding but certain parts of the inside of the gem have black [[Dissonance]] which gives it the primary color a clouded view of the interior structure, it doesn't look translucid as a Pristine state, but it doesn't have physical damage. Despite being murky, this state is usually where a [[Spellweaver]] acts with most confidence, mirroring that of [[Sectile]] [[Atonalis]] where they have rationalized enough their own wound to be fully functional but without the awareness necessary to cripple them in their own despair. [[Formless Masses]]
 
- Fractured: This is the first sign of actual damage to the [[Soul Leitmotif]], black cracks appear visible in the outer casing, not just on the inside cloudiness anymore. This state is necessary for triggering a [[Motif Awakening]] as the seeping cracks allow the [[Soul Leitmotif]] to adopt and embellish new [[Ornament]]s from the created space within. It is healthy, and almost inevitable, for a [[Spellweaver]] to reach this state but it's key to remember that any wound is merely a source of power, and what gives power can also crack you open. If the wound continues to fester it's a dangerous pivot to surrendering oneself.

- Spiraling: This is the final level before the point of no return, and it has a signature of black fractal spirals that begin to mirror the own internal chaos of the [[Spellweaver]] that is falling to the abyss of despair. The spirals on the surface are similar to [[Sky Glass]] but devoid of its beautiful tactile qualities, and this is the closest state that a [[Spellweaver]] can be to becoming an [[Atonalis]] before falling to the point of no return. **This is the last point where anyone can intervene to save them.** Any breach further on the hungering fractal spirals and the [[Soul Leitmotif]] will undergo its permanent transformation when it is fully consumed by the black of the [[Dissonance]], turning itself into a [[Dissonance Core]].

- Surrender: Once a [[Soul Leitmotif]] reaches this point, there's nothing anyone can do to save them. It has a clear indicator of two distinct crack sounds, the first is when the threshold is reached, when the [[Soul Leitmotif]] went beyond its maximum stress point, and the [[Spellweaver]] is on its last remnants of [[Coherence]] that tether their [[Composure]]. The second crack is the inevitable moment when the [[Spellweaver]] vocalizes their last words. Upon reaching this state the [[Dissonance]] cocoon emerges siphoning the user inside of it, transforming the [[Soul Leitmotif]] into the very [[Dissonance Core]] of the [[Atonalis]]. The location of the [[Dissonance Core]] is often the Wearable State of the soul gem in the last moment the dying [[Consciousness]] assigned value to anything. **The refusal to process pain feels exactly like mercy right up until the moment it permanently turns you into a predator.**

The state of the [[Soul Leitmotif]] [[Composure]] directly aligns with the internal state of mind of the [[Spellweaver]]:

A Pristine State of Mind, a Clouded State of Mind, a Fractured State of Mind, a Spiraling State of Mind, and the Surrendered State of Mind.

Despite the visual cues, these are only visible during the resting state of the [[Soul Leitmotif]]. If it's on the Wearable State, none of the Clouded or Pristine levels are visible, the only moment the [[Dissonance]] is visible on a non resting state is only until the [[Spellweaver]]'s [[Composure]] reaches Spiraling or below, and it will become visible as [[Discordant Interference]] pulsing with flickering dark alongside the color of whichever binding they're channeling.

Any real deity, like the [[Auric Aria]] or [[Outer God]]s can't become [[Atonalis]]. However, they do require [[Composure]] to function. This is particularly notable in the [[Auric Aria]] which did reach the surrender point during the [[Eighth Cycle]] and provoked the [[Lost Cycle]] for uncountable [[Cycle]]s. Her eventual return due to the pleas of [[Humanity]]gave her a sliver of [[Composure]] to move from spiraling into recovery to clouded Golden Sovereign of the [[Old Testament]].

The [[Auric Aria]] has only reached the surrendered state once, and on its very border which is why she came back to creation. Only does in the [[Alternate Hollowing]] she fully embraces the surrendered state and triggers the end of the [[Known Universe]] back into static. Typically, she hovers between spiraling at her worst, fractured on a regular, and clouded at her most vivid. Only after the sequence of the [[Singer of Paradise]], and in the apex of the [[Parlor of the Moon]] does she attain Pristine [[Composure]] after reconciliation with [[Selenea]] in the end of the [[Sonata]] of [[Arcanoria]].

### Societal Implications

Due to the [[Composure]] meter reflecting the internal state of mind of a [[Spellweaver]], there are several layers of implications on how this information is shared, externalized, or even weaponized through relationships, and even diplomacy. 

Usually the sacredness of sharing the inner view of the [[Soul Leitmotif]] is considered a moment of vulnerability, which is precisely why it's mostly equipped in the wearable state and only transformed into the resting version due to forced exhaustion, sleep, or sacred meditation. It's uncommon to have a [[Soul Leitmotif]] in a resting state without a personal guard of sorts, and it's impossible to do so without consent unless the [[Spellweaver]] physically passes out.

Even travelling parties or with allies the [[Spellweaver]] tends to keep in secret their dormant [[Soul Leitmotif]] whether in a pocket or directly by clutching it somewhere in their body during sleep. (Like hiding money under the pillow)

Furthermore, this also extends to a personal level for relationships. To deliberately invite someone to see the inside of your soul is a deeply personal and intimate gesture of courtship and romance between [[Spellweaver]]s, and in some cultures the exposure of the bare soul is indistinct from showing a naked body, which makes by proxy the dormant state as sacred as the act of physical intimacy, and to some degree both can be intertwined.

On a societal level this also reflects in diplomacy, where envoys most often than not tend to be non [[Spellweaver]]s, as [[Humanity]] without a [[Soul Leitmotif]] is useful precisely to keep undercover the internal state during the negotiations. Even if there's a [[Spellweaver]] present, most notably with any [[Head of State]], they tend to use it on the Wearable State as both class, clothing, and as means to prevent the visualization of their internal state of [[Coherence]].

However, there are some cultures that do require honesty as means to establish any formal treaty, this type of society tends to align with the [[Aureus Pillar]] or [[Waltz Pillar]]s, and they present negotiations through a pedestal where the dormant "sacred" state of a [[Soul Leitmotif]] is an anchor to the truthfulness of both parties, sometimes this technique is required in unethical practices such as torture or court trial to get information that prevents perjury due to the microscopic flashes of the [[Soul Leitmotif]] and its relationship to the [[Key of Attunement]].

This later half however does not mean a [[Spellweaver]] can't lie, on the contrary, this very basis of informational manipulation is a core tenet of [[Illusory Magic]], to bend the [[Luminance]] of a [[Soul Leitmotif]] to deliberately guide, frame, blackmail or create false evidence. The race of [[Illusory Magic]] is similar to the [[Strand]] [[Detective Magic]] applications, creating a loop of [[Spellweaving]] mastery of having measures to lie and counter measures to detect lies.

This very principle on [[Illusory Magic]] is one of the great contributions to [[The Principles of Magic]] by the partnership of [[Luminaire]] and [[Amadea]], the respective [[Mythical Virtuoso]]s of [[Luminance]] and [[Void]], the partnership gets even pushed further with [[Cordelia]] making the intersection of these [[Mythical Virtuoso]] the founding school of proper [[Illusory Magic]] and [[Detective Magic]].

The implications of having a visual cue to the [[Soul Leitmotif]] is both important religion, diplomacy, and culture wise, heavily varying on the interpretation of the [[Pillars]] of [[Civilization]]. Lying becomes much more sophisticated and hard to identify if the evidence itself can be contradictory.

# Consciousness

#spellweaving

*The ink which writes [[The Eternal Symphony]]*.

An abstract form of raw existence, it is one of the most essential concepts for giving form into matter and energy from chaos, thus [[Mastery Over Chaos]] being the principal method of transforming reality.

It exists in all of [[The Infinite Void]], and emerges as a variation of it as a structured deterministic pattern in [[The First Overtone]]. Ironically, it is a diluted version of [[Primal White Noise]] that has stabilized into existence as a [[Fundamental Frequency]].

Crystalized [[Consciousness]] is the primary element of [[Crystal]] and reflects this as the laws of quantum collapse in the [[Auric Heptacode]].

# Consensual Anchoring

_"That wall is, in fact, invisible" - [[Puppet Master]] [[Luminance]] [[Spellweaver]]_

A delusion can sustain [[Signal Loss]] if you can exchange which [[Consciousness]] believes in the spell. This is a [[Crystal]] / [[Luminance]] / [[Flux]] interaction where [[Stable Harmonic Channels]] form if the caster can deceive or force the target to also believe the illusion is real.

It is a funding principle of [[Illusory Magic]] that says that combat is as much of a battle of technical mastery and sheer imagination as it is of psychological dominance.

**Narrative Applications:**

- A city where everyone believes a lie—the lie becomes true
- An illusionist who's gathered a cult to make their illusions permanent
- The horror of realizing your own disbelief is _hurting_ someone—if you stop believing in their protective illusion, it fails

# Consonance

Order and harmony, what is the natural "good" for in [[Arcanoria]]. The opposite of [[Dissonance]].

# Constellation

_"Death is just the day of the publication of your [[Magnum Opus]]."_

A [[Legend]] that has ascended to the [[Stellar Legacy Score]]. They can form a variety of [[Stellar Covenant]]s. [[Outer God]]s and actual deities can't be [[Constellation]]s, they have to be [[Legend]]s exclusively.

All [[Constellation]]s live in a spectrum between [[Constellation]]s of [[Consonance]] and [[Constellation]]s of [[Dissonance]]. This alignment depends on whether they were "good" or "evil" during their lifetime as a [[Legend]]. The specific alignment depends on the type of [[Legend Opus]] and [[Legend Title]]s they have:

- [[Constellation]] of pure [[Consonance]]: [[Mira]] given that they were pretty selfless in their life, and did genuine good for those dying while she herself suffered the same condition. Her offer to [[Lacrimosa]] was also born from a place of [[Consonance]].
  
- [[Constellation]] of pure [[Dissonance]]: [[Syvanth]] which is the complete opposite as his [[Legend]] came to be born as the Killer of the Great Expanse and whose [[Legend]] is the ominous [[Ballad]] sung after his horrific beautification.
  
- Mixture of [[Consonance]] and [[Dissonance]]: [[Cadmus Tacet]] which is a complex moral character as he had great [[Legend Opus]] like the Scalpel of [[Humanity]]'s Hope, but also horrific [[Legend Title]]s due to the means he used to achieve said goals, like The Vivisector due to his brutal methods on mapping the [[Pure Light]] spectrum. Most [[Constellation]]s are placed in this bracket as a mixture of both.

Depending on the specific pairings on which [[Constellation]]s are receiving [[Constellation Worship]], they can unlock several effects, and the mixture between [[Consonance]] and [[Dissonance]] is a fertile ground for friction and unique [[Syncretism]]. Furthermore, [[Constellation]]s can change their affinity to either [[Consonance]] or [[Dissonance]] through [[Mythic Drift]] by adapting to the new ways on which they receive their specific [[Constellation Worship]].

Finally, [[Constellation]]s of great [[Constellation Renown]] and [[Constellation Worship]] can have the ability of [[Reincarnation]] due to having a strong tether between [[Arcanoria]] and [[The Eternal Symphony]]. This allows a character to be reborn in [[Ages]] different from the ones in their original mythos. They receive some bonus to their starting [[Legend Trait]]s based on their defining [[Constellation]], but are effectively "reset" of all their memories and previous titles. They are a blank canvas that shares the same character [[Soul-Key]] and name, considering both their original starting [[Legend Trait]]s and physical looks. They are back the moment before they began their original [[Legend]]. Moreover, some [[Dissonance]] [[Legend Trait]]s can be removed of their origin to accommodate to a new life. For example, removing "Orphan" from [[Mira]] since she has an actual family now.

[[Reincarnation]] is a mechanic destined to give the [[Civilization]] a chance to grow a stronger [[Constellation]] through [[Syncretism]] and give them a different "ending" with unique [[Legend Opus]] and different [[Legend Trait]]s. For example, if they worship [[Mira]], she can reincarnate during [[Ages]] XI as a magical girl during the [[Age of Starlight]] to give her a chance of a life without that much suffering as an orphan. Of course, whenever a [[Constellation]] is undergoing [[Reincarnation]], they are not available to the [[Stellar Legacy Score]] until they die again and become a [[Constellation]] with the new set of [[Legend Opus]] and [[Legend Title]]s. Their specific [[World Truth]]s however will be permanent independent of whether they are in [[Reincarnation]]. They just can't form [[Stellar Covenant]]s for the [[Ages]] where they experience being a mortal because they're temporarily not a [[Constellation]] anymore.

[[Reincarnation]] can only be triggered after the [[Constellation]] has experienced at least three [[Ages]] being a [[Constellation]]. Furthermore, the process itself is costly and requires a strong tether of [[Resonance]] between [[Arcanoria]] and [[The Eternal Symphony]]. Thus, [[Reincarnation]] can only happen during an [[Age Transition]], and its dependent on the slots [[Civilization]] has unlocked for [[Reincarnation]]. The default state is up to two concurrent [[Reincarnation]]s but after learning [[The Truth of Arcanoria]] the slots can be expanded and its cooldowns of three [[Ages]] can be reduced.
