# Great Harmonic Loom

#technology

![[Great Harmonic Loom.png]]

An enormous construct suspended between the physicality of [[Arcanoria]], the mortal realm, and the sea of cosmic void. The structure was woven by the [[Auric Aria]] during the [[Second Cycle]] as the magical framework for channeling [[Resonance]] and giving structure to [[Consciousness]]. This vast weave and [[Flux]]-vibrational membrane spreads through [[Arcanoria]]'s upper atmosphere, fifteen to twenty-five leagues above the surface, where it stratifies not by temperature or wind, but by [[Vibrational Density]] — the measure of how tightly reality's threads maintain their harmonic integrity. [[Syvanth]]

### The Architecture of Harmonized Reality

The [[Great Harmonic Loom]] manifests as a living lattice of the [[Auric Heptacode]]'s sevenfold golden threads, each existing in [[Superposed Resonance]] — a state where all possible notes ring simultaneously until [[Consciousness]] collapses them into a singular sound. Such creates [[Harmonic Entanglement]] that couples all of the disparate vibrations across impossible distances, binding thought to form and delimiting probability and feasibility as sympathetic musical [[Resonance]].

Unlike the physicality of the lower atmospheric layers that separate by material, mortal properties, the [[Great Harmonic Loom]] stratifies by its [[Grand Thread Rings]], much as tectonic plates shift, so do these rings realign under [[Cosmic Motion]]. Where [[Coherence]] runs deep, magic flows easily through the [[Stable Harmonic Channels]]. Where it fractures, it produces [[Discordant Interference]] — chaotic vibrations that rend the interwoven strings and contaminate spells with [[Primal White Noise]], causing them to fail, backfire, or manifest unpredictably. This failure occurs because broken [[Coherence]] cannot sustain the focused intent required by [[The Principles of Magic]].

Likewise, the [[Trinity Harmony]] governs this temporal [[Coherence]]: past emotional states create standing wave patterns that either amplify or dampen present magical attempts. At the same time, future potentials exist as [[Probability Amplitudes]] awaiting [[Consciousness]] to collapse them into certainty. This temporal layering explains why a practitioner's emotional history and mental state directly affect spell stability and potency.

### The Symphonic Veins and Lunar Sorrow

Threading through this spectral membrane, the [[Leylines]] function as harmonic conduits — channels where [[Vibrational Density]] reaches its peak, allowing magical effects to propagate across vast distances with minimal [[Vibrational Decay]]. These [[Symphonic Veins]] in turn carry not wind or water, but [[Coherence]] itself encoded in discrete information packages called [[Frequency Harmonics]], and act as the preferential pathways for spellcraft governed by [[The Principles of Magic]].

The [[Great Harmonic Loom]]'s connection to [[Selenea]]'s imprisonment permeates its structure with a constant sorrow. Her bound essence leaks [[Lunehymn]] as liquid [[Coherence]] that enhances the membrane's probability stability during lunar phases when her melancholy runs strongest. [[Emberwhisper]] crystals, formed from her crystallized grief, serve as the primary [[Resonance Anchors]] within the Loom, providing stable reference points to maintain spell [[Coherence]] over distance and time.

### The Mortal Interface: Where Flesh Meets Symphony

![[Great Harmonic Loom-1.png]]

All magical capacity arises when any [[Consciousness]] — beast, mortal, or spirit — attunes its [[Fundamental Frequency]] to the [[Great Harmonic Loom]]’s baseline in [[Consonance]] with the [[Auric Aria]]’s vibrational signature. Heightened emotion shapes that [[Resonance]] into a standing‑wave pattern, where prior feelings amplify or dampen the present signal within the [[Flux]]‑vibrational membrane, establishing [[Sympathetic Vibration]] as the imbuing of feeling into the coupling and enabling to phase‑lock with the [[Grand Thread Rings]].​

Once phase‑locked, focused intention selects a target mode, collapsing [[Superposed Resonance]] as the effective “pluck” of specific threads of the [[Great Harmonic Loom]], creating localized field perturbations that propagate only through regions of strong [[Coherence]] along [[Stable Harmonic Channels]] that then manifest as magical effects.​

The first [[Attunement for Magic]], achieved when compassion touched the wounded [[Auric Aria]], established this [[Flux]] coupling; their shared sorrow created the precise emotional frequency necessary for [[Coherence]] to interact with the [[Great Harmonic Loom]]’s structure. Thus, this proves that magic requires as much [[Potential of Creation]] as it does [[Mastery Over Chaos]], and, without both elements and a proper [[Key of Attunement]], the [[Spellweaver]] cannot achieve the psychophysical alignment necessary to sustain predictable [[Spellweaving]].

The whole process of casting magic behaves like a full audio signal chain and requires the following steps:

1. [[Resonance]] as the vibration of a [[Fundamental Frequency]] to create a signal. This raw carrier wave is a pure tone that becomes the baseband signal.

2. A [[Spellweaving]] interface that acts as a transducer of the internal psychophysical vibration. It is the object bridging the physical and metaphysical, like a [[Soul Leitmotif]] or an organ with [[Coherence Binding Tissue]], which then is able to encode encode said signal into [[Frequency Harmonics]] and phase-lock with the [[Great Harmonic Loom]]. Without this interface, the [[Resonance]] never becomes a [[Coherence]]-filled, multiplexable signal in the [[Great Harmonic Loom]]. This is what defines who and what is a [[Spellweaver]].

3. [[Attunement for Magic]] where the [[Key of Attunement]] comes in as carrier integrity and spectral cleanup. It ensures the [[Consonance]] of that [[Resonance]] frequency with the [[Auric Aria]]'s own [[Fundamental Frequency]]. Symbolically, it is essentially "feeling the music" so deeply that your own [[Soul-Key]] resonates with it, and thus that consonance becomes as much you as it is the song you are playing in the moment. It mechanically "cleans-up" the signal of [[Spellweaving]] by having a correct center with the broadcast standard.

4. Enrichment of the signal through [[The Principles of Magic]]. It is the phase that adds modulation as a synthesis chain that sculpts the spell, adding texture and complexity to the original [[Resonance]] by imbuing the characteristics of [[Spellweaving]], like potency, effect, power, area, and intent through [[Mastery Over Chaos]] and [[Potential of Creation]]. The specific effects are:

### THE THREE WAVES: PROGRESSION OF CONTINENTAL CATASTROPHE

**WAVE I: THE SILENT VECTORS (Month 0-12)

**Outbreak zones**: Capitals, major settlements, trade nodes (high-[[Confluence]] zones with heavy extractor activity)
**Confluence saturation**: 5-25% (low, but above dormancy threshold)
**Disease manifestation**: Manifestation 1 (Consumption) dominates; some early Manifestation 2 at zone edges

**Trigger event**:

- Great Hunger relief festival causes massive synchronized spellcasting
- [[Leylines]] extraction spikes from 30-40% to 60-70% baseline saturation temporarily
- This spike activates [[Fungal Matriarch]] spores globally through [[Leylines]] propagation
- First infections appear in festival capitals.

**What's actually happening**:

- Bacterial colonization proceeds slowly (low magical energy available)
- [[EC]] production is gradual; immune system can partially fight
- Symptoms are visible and recognizable: respiratory illness
- Deaths are spread over weeks (not clustered epidemically)
- Sweet smell is detectable but faint
    

**Why moth vector remains invisible**:

- Disease looks like natural consumption/tuberculosis
- Aromatics seem to help (by accident, through social isolation of suspected cases)
- Authorities gain false confidence they understand the disease
- [[Luminant Moths]] populations are growing but not yet obviously problematic
- No [[Dissonance Bloom]] effects (low saturation)
- No [[Static Criticality]] cascades (saturation too low)

**Authority response**:

- Identifies disease as consumption (partially correct)
- Implements aromatics (completely ineffective but seems helpful)
- Quarantines visible cases (accidentally useful)
- Confidence increases because some people recover

**Mortality**: 25-40% in affected capitals over 12 months; spreads via refugee and trade networks

**Outcome**: Wave I subsides in origin capitals as saturation stabilizes; false confidence spreads; infected refugees carry disease + massive moth populations to secondary cities


**WAVE II: ESCALATION & INFRASTRUCTURE CASCADE (Month 12-36)

**Phase A: Initial Escalation in Refugee Zones (Month 12-18)

**Outbreak zones**: Refugee settlements, trade hubs, secondary cities (receiving refugee populations)

**Confluence saturation**: 40-55% (baseline + refugee moths + continued extraction)

**Disease manifestation**: Consumption → transition to Dancing Plague

**What happens**:

- Refugees fleeing capitals carry infection + massive moth populations
- Refugee camps concentrate high-saturation conditions
- New infections occur in refugee populations
- Moderate saturation accelerates bacterial growth
- Manifestation 2 (Dancing Plague) begins emerging in camps
    

**In refugee camps**:

- Newly infected reach Stage 2 quickly (4-7 days)
- [[EC]] production is substantial and magical resonance becomes pronounced
- Motor hijacking begins; compulsive movement starts
- [[Dissonance ]]radiates from each dancer
- Exponential recruitment: 1 dancer → 5 → 50 → 500+ within days

**Authority response**:

- Observe dancing; conclude "possession or madness"
- Escalate aromatics (incorrect response)
- Fumigate (kills outdoor moths; drives remaining indoors)
- Attempt isolation (confounded by [[Dissonance]] attraction)

**Infrastructure stress begins**:

- Deaths reach 40-50% in refugee camps
- Maintenance staff for extractors are dead/unavailable/quarantined
- Extractors continue operating without regulation
- [[Dual Confluence Stream]] imbalance accumulates in storage/distribution systems
- Baseline saturation rises from 40-50% toward 55-65%

**Mortality**: 50-60% in refugee zones over 6 months

**Phase B: Infrastructure Failure & First Cascades (Month 18-30)

**Outbreak zones**: Secondary cities, extraction sites (where infrastructure is failing)
**Confluence saturation**: 60-75% (accumulation from unmaintained extractors + continued refugee influx)
**Disease manifestation**: Manifestation 2-3 boundary; Frenzy beginning

**What happens**:

- Unmaintained extractors accumulate [[Dual Confluence Stream]] without operational release
- Saturation spikes from 55% to 65-75% in multiple zones
- Some extractor systems rupture; magic spills uncontrolled
- Newly infected individuals reach Manifestation 3 threshold (asymptomatic frenzy)
- First [[Static Criticality]] cascades occur
    

**First cascade events**:

- Infected person in Frenzy stage enters high-saturation zone
- Motor seizure + [[Dissonance]] + person's conductive nervous system
- Local saturation is 70%+ (near cascade threshold)
- System tips past equilibrium
- [[Static Criticality]] fires

**What cascade event does**:

- Raw [[Aetherlight]] discharges through conductive paths (person's nervous system, extractors, ground)
- Person and nearby [[Luminant Moths]] vaporized instantly
- Ground ruptures in 20-30m radius
- Releases [[Aetherlight]] into atmosphere
- Creates temporary anti-magic zone ([[Coherence]] too fractured for new spellcasting)
- Releases [[Emberwhisper]] particles into upper atmosphere
    

**Cascade frequency**:

- Month 18-24: Cascade every few days (triggered only by Manifestation 3 individuals in peak zones)
- Month 24-30: Cascade every 1-2 days (infrastructure failures now also triggering)

**Infrastructure effects**:

- Extractors damaged by cascades
- Authority attempts to activate additional extractors (to compensate for lost ones)
- More extractors = more demand = higher saturation = more cascades = vicious cycle

**Emberwhisper fallout begins** (Month 24+):

- Cascades release [[Aetherlight]]
- Particles accumulate in atmosphere
- Visible shimmer/pale glow in sky develops
- Fallout rain begins (appears as warm, iridescent droplets)

**Cascade consequence—secondary cascade**:

- [[Emberwhisper]] particles fall as rain
- Particles destabilize on soil contact
- Rain detonates on impact: secondary explosion
- Raises saturation further (72% → 75% → 78%)

**Mortality**: 60-80% in secondary cities over 18 months

**Phase C: Systemic Failure (Month 30-36)

**Outbreak zones**: All high-saturation zones simultaneously
**Confluence saturation**: 75-85% (critical cascade zone; approaching spontaneous cascade point)
**Disease manifestation**: Manifestation 3 dominant

**What happens**:

- Saturation approaches tipping point in multiple regions
- Cascades become regular occurrence (daily or multiple times daily)
- Infrastructure is largely destroyed or abandoned
- [[Emberwhisper]] fallout becomes continuous
- Ground is hazardous (detonates when rain falls) and triggers [[Vibrational Fallout]].

**Cascade sources multiply**:

- Infected individuals (fewer remaining, but still occurring)
- Residual [[EC]] in soil triggering secondary cascades of [[Vibrational Fallout]] (weeks after infected person dies) while becoming a new infection point.
- **Unmaintained extractors rupturing** under accumulated pressure
- **[[Leylines]] ruptures cascading** (geometric spread of damage)

**Authority collapse**:

- Confidence in response completely shattered
- Authority structures destroyed (officials dead, fled, or powerless)
- Some regions turn to prayer/ritual
- Others attempt radical measures (burning quarters, forced extermination)
- All measures fail
    

**Environmental deterioration**:

- Ground becomes contaminated by [[Vibrational Fallout]].
- [[Emberwhisper]] pure embers poisons water supplies
- Regions become increasingly uninhabitable
- Survivors flee or die
    

**Mortality**: 70-85% in high-saturation zones over 36 months

**WAVE III: ENDEMIC PHASE & ADAPTATION (Month 36+)

By month 36, plague has transitioned from epidemic to **endemic status**. All regions are simultaneously affected; no new populations to infect. Regional outcomes diverge sharply based on the [[Dual Confluence Stream]] saturation:

**Low-Saturation Zones (5-40% imbalance)

**Disease manifestation**: Manifestation 1 (Consumption) only

**Cascade risk**: None (saturation too low)

**Outcome**:

- Plague becomes endemic disease, not epidemic
- 2-5% annual mortality (manageable)
- Civilization continues in reduced form
- Life is disrupted but functional
- Some settlements thrive relative to others
- No [[Static Criticality]] hazard
    

**Why these zones survive**:

- Saturation too low for cascade threshold
- No [[Dissonance]] bloom (slow-progression manifestation)
- Disease kills slowly over 1-2 weeks
- Bodies can be buried safely
- Survivors develop some acquired immunity/resilience

**Moderate-Saturation Zones (40-75% imbalance)

**Disease manifestation**: Manifestation 1-2 boundary

**Cascade risk**: Episodic (weekly or monthly, not constant)

**Outcome**:

- Cascades occur but are not constant
- Infection rate stabilizes to endemic level
- Some settlements attempt partial extractor operation (at reduced capacity)
- Authority figures implement regulations to prevent saturation spikes
- Communities learn to coexist with both endemic plague and periodic cascade hazard

**Why civilization survives here**:

- Saturation below spontaneous cascade point
- Careful management can prevent tipping
- Extractors can be maintained at lower operational levels
- [[Emberwhisper]] fallout manageable (hazardous but not continuous)
    

**High-Saturation Zones (75%+ imbalance)

**Disease manifestation**: Manifestation 2-3

**Cascade risk**: Constant (multiple cascades daily; approaching spontaneous cascade point)

**Outcome**:

- Cascades are daily occurrence
- Infrastructure is destroyed
- Cascades occur from multiple sources simultaneously
- Saturation approaches or exceeds spontaneous cascade threshold (90%+ imbalance)
- Regions become uninhabitable except for brief visits
- These become the "Wasted Zones" of the [[Age of Embers]]

**Eventually**:

- Saturation exceeds 90%
- System cascades spontaneously without any trigger
- Continuous [[Aetherlight]] discharge from [[Leylines]]
- [[Emberwhisper]] rain is constant
- Ground continuously detonates
- [[Civilization]] requires underground shelters

**Outcome**: 70-85% mortality in high-saturation zones; wastelands form; survivors become nomadic or flee to adapted zones

### THE HISTORICAL PARALLELS

**The Black Plague (1347-1353)

- **Vector**: Fleas on rats (invisible to medieval authorities)
- **Observed symptom**: Sweet smell of decomposition (tissue necrosis)
- **Authority response**: Aromatic masks, burning herbs, fumigation
- **Root cause misunderstood**: Miasma theory (bad air) instead of flea-borne transmission
- **Death toll**: 75-200 million people (25-60% of European population)
- **Outcome**: Institutional collapse; labor shortage; social upheaval; feudalism weakened

**How [[Luminant Rot]] mirrors this**:

- **Vector**: [[Luminant Moths]] (invisible to authorities; beloved instead of hated) and the [[Fungal Matriarch]] is the secret killer albeit harmless on its own.
- **Observed symptom**: Sweet smell from [[EC]] production (similar to Black Plague decomposition smell)
- **Authority response**: Identical—aromatic masks, burning incense, fumigation
- **Root cause misunderstood**: Miasma theory (bad air) instead of moth-borne transmission
- **Death toll**: 60-85% of continent's population (depending on region)
- **Outcome**: Identical—institutional collapse; labor shortage; social upheaval; civilization reverts to lower-magic living

**Unique difference**: Unlike Black Plague (natural catastrophe, unprecedented), [[Luminant Rot]] is partly self-inflicted. Civilization engineered the high-[[Dual Confluence Stream]] zones that activate dormant [[Fungal Matriarch]]s.

**The Dancing Plague of 1518 (Strasbourg)

- **Vector**: Ergot poisoning (fungal contamination of grain—Claviceps purpurea)
- **Symptoms**: Compulsive dancing; exhaustion; death (15% mortality among afflicted)
- **Mechanism**: Real neurological toxin (ergotamine; LSD precursor causes vasoconstriction)
- **Contributing factors**: Mass hysteria; religious fervor; psychological contagion
- **Outcome**: Unknown endpoint; plague subsided after weeks

**How Manifestation 2 (Dancing Plague) mirrors this**:

- **Vector**: [[EC]] produced by activated [[Luminant Decay]] bacteria (real neurological toxin)
- **Symptoms**: Compulsive dancing; euphoria; exhaustion; death
- **Mechanism**: Real neurological hijacking + magical amplification
- **Contributing factors**: [[Dissonance]] (magical contagion field); psychological + magical interaction
- **Outcome**: Exponential spread; continues until saturation changes

**Critical difference**: The Euphoria Plague is genuinely bio-magical. It's not pure psychology or hallucination—the [[Dissonance]] bloom is a real magical field that compels movement.

### Narrative Timeline

**Pacing Checklist:

-  Turns 0-5: Disease emerges (feels manageable)
-  Turns 5-15: Sweet smell identified (seems like solution point)
-  Turns 10-20: Aromatics implemented (false confidence peaks)
-  Turns 15-25: Aromatic solution begins failing (first reality check)
-  Turns 20-30: Dancing emerges (new problem? or same problem?)
-  Turns 25-35: Dancing recruits exponentially (mysterious and wrong)
-  Turns 30-40: Moths revealed as correlation (solution appears!)
-  Turns 35-50: Moth control strategy (consuming resources, seeming to help)
-  Turns 50-60: Moth control fails (second failure)
-  Turn 60: CASCADE EVENT (tonal shift from crisis to apocalypse)
-  Turns 60-70: Euphoria Fracture intensifies (understanding dawns)

**Discovery Layer 1: Disease (Turns 0-20)

**What's True:** Respiratory illness exists, sweet smell IS a marker  
**What's False:** Sweet smell is the vector  
**What's Missing:** The deeper cause

**Discovery Layer 2: Vectors (Turns 20-50)

**What's True:** Moths ARE carrying bacteria  
**What's False:** Moths are the root cause  
**What's Missing:** Saturation mechanism, extraction patterns

**Discovery Layer 3: Saturation (Turns 50-70)

**What's True:** Magical saturation IS rising and IS causing symptoms  
**What's False:** The cause is unclear (seems like natural phenomenon)  
**What's Missing:** Civilization's role in creating it

**Discovery Layer 4: Harmonic Imbalance (Turns 70-75)

**What's True:** Aetherlight and Lunehymn imbalance IS the mechanism  
**What's False:** Solving it is difficult but possible (true, but incomplete)  
**What's Missing:** Why imbalance occurred (extraction patterns), why moths died (fumigation)

**Complete Understanding (Post-Game)

**The Full Picture:**

1. Pre-plague: Civilization extracted Aetherlight and Lunehymn unevenly
2. Luminant Moths naturally metabolized excess saturation (natural balance mechanism)
3. Civilization loved the moths (beautiful, useful, culturally important) and expanded farming
4. Fumigation and moth farming disrupted populations
5. Balance mechanism failed
6. Saturation accumulated
7. Fungal Matriarch (dormant for ages) activated at saturation 25
8. All three manifestations emerged from single root cause
9. Deep lesson: Civilization's love of light and magic created the very catastrophe it feared

**ACT I: THE MYSTERIOUS ILLNESS (Turns 0-20, Saturation 5-25)

Turns 0-5: "A Cough Appears"

**Event:** Respiratory illness in capital cities

**What Players See:**

- Visible: Fever, cough, death (8-14 day progression)
    
- Mortality: 40-50%
    
- Flavor: "Physicians believe this is consumption, like our ancestors faced"
    

**What's Hidden:**

- Saturation rising from 5 → 15 (invisible meter)
    
- Fungal Matriarch spores germinating (invisible)
    
- Luminant Decay bacteria dormant in moth populations (invisible)
    

**Player Psychology:** "Medical crisis. Treat it like a disease."

Turns 5-10: "The Sweet Smell Emerges"

**Event:** Infected persons exhale sweet-smelling compounds

**What Players See:**

- Observable pattern: sweet smell correlates with infection
    
- Flavor: "The sweet smell. Some believe it's the disease itself, carried through air."
    
- First aromatic masks distributed
    
- "The smell is miasmic—we must prevent exposure to it"
    

**Hidden Truth:**

- Sweet smell IS real (EC production from bacterial metabolism)
    
- But it's NOT contagious (it's an internal chemical, not external vector)
    
- Saturation 15 → 25
    
- Fungal Matriarch beginning global activation through Leyline network
    

**Player Conclusion:** "The sweet smell is the vector. Control the smell, control the disease."

**This is the first logical but incomplete conclusion.** Players have identified a real symptom and misinterpreted it as cause.

Turns 10-20: "The Aromatic Solution Works!"

**Event:** Aromatic masks distributed widely

**What Players See:**

- Regions with masking show reduced infection
    
- Flavor: "The aromatic masks appear effective. The council celebrates."
    
- Player gains confidence
    
- Expansion of aromatic treatment nationwide
    

**Hidden Tragedy:**

- Saturation 25 → 35
    
- Fungal Matriarch spores activate globally (simultaneous across all Leylines)
    
- Atmospheric fumigation KILLS outdoor Luminant Moths (unintended consequence)
    
- Indoor moth populations explode 10x (insects flee treated areas)
    
- Luminant Decay bacteria becoming increasingly virulent as fungal metabolites accumulate
    

**Player Psychology:** "Success! We understand the problem and we're solving it!"

**Pacing Note:** This is peak false confidence. Everything feels under control. But cascade failure is building invisibly.

**ACT II: THE HIDDEN ESCALATION (Turns 20-50, Saturation 40-70)

Turns 20-30: "Strange Movements Appear"

**THIS IS THE CRITICAL MISDIRECTION POINT.**

**Event:** Compulsive dancing emerges in some settlements

**What Players See:**

- Different cities report: "Citizens moving compulsively. Dancing involuntarily. No apparent cause."
    
- NOT immediately obvious this is related to the respiratory plague
    
- Flavor: "Some physicians believe this is possession. Others propose mass hysteria. A psychological phenomenon, perhaps."
    
- Different debuff from disease (Emotional Unrest vs. Sickness)
    
- Different resource costs to address
    

**Hidden Truth:**

- THIS IS MANIFESTATION 2 of the same plague
    
- Saturation 40 → 50
    
- Moderate saturation level causes neurological hijacking via EC production
    
- Dissonance bloom is beginning (magical field effect, not biological contagion)
    
- Players don't realize this is disease because it has no visible infection vector
    

**Player Psychology:** "We have TWO problems now. Disease AND emotional unrest. Or... are they related?"

**Design Insight:** Don't hint at connection. Let players think they're managing separate crises. This makes the later revelation (they're one system) shocking.

Turns 25-35: "Exponential Dancing Recruitment"

**Event:** Dancing spreads exponentially

**What Players See:**

- 1 dancer in marketplace
    
- 24 hours later: 5-10 dancers
    
- 48 hours later: 50 dancers
    
- 72 hours later: entire marketplace is dancing
    
- Exponential growth, not linear spread
    
- Isolation attempts fail (people in proximity become infected despite barriers)
    

**New Understanding:** "This isn't normal disease transmission."

**Event: "The Moths Are Everywhere"** (Turn 35-40)

Scholars notice: Moth populations have exploded in high-infection regions.

**What Gets Revealed:**

- Moth population meter becomes visible
    
- Correlation with both disease AND dancing is obvious
    
- "These creatures were always here. But now... everywhere the plague is worst, moths are most abundant."
    

**Player Conclusion:** "AH! The moths are the vector! They carry the bacteria from person to person!"

**Hidden Truth:**

- Saturation 50 → 60
    
- Dissonance bloom recruiting exponentially (is magnetic/magical, not biological)
    
- EC production at threshold where euphoria-like symptoms emerge
    
- Cascades forming invisibly (not yet visible, but saturation is near cascade threshold)
    
- **The moth-vector theory is PARTIALLY TRUE but MISLEADING**
    
    - Moths ARE carrying bacteria (true)
        
    - But moths aren't the root cause; they're the MECHANISM through which saturation expresses as disease
        
    - Controlling moths won't solve the problem (which is saturation itself)
        

**Player Psychology:** "Finally! We understand. The moths are the answer. Eliminate moths = eliminate plague."

**Critical Design:** Make the moth theory seem obviously correct. This keeps player focused on wrong solution while true crisis (saturation/Harmonic Imbalance) accumulates invisibly.

Turns 35-50: "The Moth Control Strategy"

**Event: "The Great Moth Cull"**

Player chooses moth control approach:

- Fumigation (kills outdoor moths)
    
- Pesticides (broad approach)
    
- Farming restrictions (reduce domesticated populations)
    
- Complete elimination (radical, civilization penalty)
    

**What Players See:**

- Outdoor moth populations declining (visible on map)
    
- Some regions show reduced disease
    
- Flavor: "The moth control initiative shows promise in some regions."
    
- Resource cost is high but seems worthwhile
    

**Hidden Truth:**

- Saturation 60 → 70 (approaching critical threshold)
    
- Outdoor fumigation kills susceptible moths
    
- **Survivors driven indoors where people remove masks in private spaces**
    
- Indoor moth populations multiplying rapidly (10x, invisible to player)
    
- Infrastructure maintenance requires increased extraction (to compensate for light loss)
    
- **Extraction raising saturation further (vicious cycle invisible to player)**
    

**Player Psychology:** "The strategy is working. But at great cost. Should we continue?"

**ACT III: THE APOCALYPTIC REVELATION (Turns 50-75, Saturation 70-95)

Turns 50-60: "Moth Control Fails"

**Event: "Disease Continues Despite Moth Control"**

**What Players See:**

- Disease still spreading in regions with strongest moth control
    
- Flavor: "Physicians are baffled. The moth theory should have worked."
    
- Resource expenditure has been massive
    
- Result: Minimal benefit
    

**Event: "Widespread Euphoria"** (Emerging alongside disease failure)

**New Phenomenon:** Citizens report "unusual happiness without cause"

- "Everything is bright and beautiful"
    
- "I feel wonderful for no reason"
    
- "The world is perfect"
    

**What's Happening:** Saturation 70 → 75, Euphoria Fracture beginning

**Critical Moment: Euphoria Is NOT Connected to Disease**

- Flavor text treats it as separate phenomenon
    
- No obvious connection to the plague
    
- Seems like civilization is experiencing something positive?
    
- But happiness is building as crisis deepens
    

**Player Realization:** "The moth theory was wrong. Something else is happening."

Turns 55-65: "The Cascades Return"

**Event: "The Sky Ignites"** (Turn 60, THE TONAL PIVOT)

**This is the moment everything changes.**

**What Players Experience:**

- Explosion of magical force in high-saturation city
    
- Ground rupture, 20-30m radius destruction
    
- Cascade of magical energy erupts into sky
    
- Iridescent particles fall as rain
    
- Where rain touches: secondary explosions
    

**Saturation Meter Becomes Visible (First Time)**

Shows:

- Current saturation in each region (70-75)
    
- Historical peak (red line at pre-plague level)
    
- Critical threshold (red zone at 75+)
    
- Direction: RISING
    

**Player Realization:**  
"This is NOT a disease. This is MAGICAL. The problem is magical saturation, not biological infection. All our solutions were addressing the wrong problem."

**The Complete Failure Moment:**

- Disease theory: Wrong (but there WAS a disease)
    
- Aromatic theory: Wrong (but there WAS a sweet smell)
    
- Moth theory: Wrong (but there WERE moth vectors)
    
- True problem: **Harmonic Imbalance in Dual Confluence Stream**
    
- Rising saturation from civilization's extraction patterns
    

**Player Psychology:** Horror, realization, desperation.

Turns 60-70: "The Euphoria Fracture in Full Swing"

**Event: "The Euphoria Intensifies"**

**What Players See:**

- Euphoria spreading civilization-wide
    
- Genuine happiness, compulsive movement (dancing)
    
- Citizens describe: "I feel transcendent. Everything is perfect. I don't want this to end."
    
- Flavor: "The euphoria is intensifying. Citizens are experiencing genuine joy despite cascades occurring."
    

**The Paradox:** Citizens are happiest while catastrophe unfolds.

**Event: "Cascades Multiply"** (Every 1-2 turns)

- Explosions of magical force in high-saturation zones
    
- Emberwhisper rain constant
    
- Ground detonating (secondary cascades)
    
- Infrastructure being destroyed faster than it can be repaired
    
- **Cascades kill exponentially more than the original plague**
    

**What's Actually Happening:**

**Saturation 75 → 90:**

This isn't just disease manifestation anymore—this is **pure magical overflow euphoria**, separate from (but happening alongside) the Frenzy manifestation.

- EC in soil + water activating from magical overflow (not just bacterial source)
    
- Aetherlight and Lunehymn both overflowing (Harmonic Imbalance)
    
- Static Criticality cascades reaching critical frequency
    
- **Euphoria Fracture:** Civilization-wide euphoria from magical overflow, not disease
    

**The Catastrophic Feedback Loop:**

1. Saturation high → Cascades increase
    
2. Cascades damage infrastructure
    
3. Authorities try to repair/maintain extractors
    
4. Extraction raises saturation further
    
5. More cascades
    
6. Loop intensifies, vicious cycle locks in
    
Turns 65-75: "The Decision Point and Outcome"

**Critical Event: "The World Hangs in Balance"** (Turn 65)

### Crisis Metrics

**METRIC 1: Population Viability

**Measurement:** Percentage of starting population surviving Turn 75

**Baseline at Turn 0:** 100%

**Population Loss Mechanics

**Early Crisis (Turns 0-50): Consumption Manifestation**

- Per affected city per turn: -0.2% baseline population loss
    
- With Plague Doctor Department: -0.15% (mitigated)
    
- With Quarantine Centers: -0.1% (further mitigated)
    
- **Turns 0-50: Total potential loss 0-10%** (depending on mitigation)
    

**Mid Crisis (Turns 20-70): Dancing Plague / Frenzy**

- Adds -0.5% per turn in affected cities
    
- No direct mitigation for compulsive movement
    
- But morale management prevents civil panic losses
    

**Late Crisis (Turns 60-75): Cascades and Euphoria Fracture**

- Per cascade event: -1-3% population in affected zone
    
- 5-10 cascades total
    
- Plus euphoria complications: -0.5-1% per turn
    
- **Turns 60-75: 5-15% additional population loss**
    

**Additional Loss Vectors:**

- **Starvation Deaths** (if agricultural stabilization not active): -0.5% per turn during crisis = 5% total
    
- **Migration Chaos** (if morale below 40%): -2-3% concentrated in receiving zones
    
- **Civil Unrest** (if institutional trust below 30%): -1-2% per turn from riots/violence
    
- **Infrastructure Collapse** (if cascade damage not managed): cascading morale losses leading to -0.5% per turn

|Outcome|Population Remaining|Total Loss|Causes|
|---|---|---|---|
|Age of Behemoths|75%|25%|Unavoidable disease (20%) + minimal avoidable losses (5%)|
|Age of Glyphs|60%|40%|Unavoidable disease (20%) + some avoidable losses (20%)|
|Age of Embers|30-35%|65-70%|Unavoidable disease (20%) + all avoidable losses (45-50%)|

**METRIC 2: Institutional Trust

**Measurement:** Percentage trust in government/authorities (visible on UI from Turn 40+)

**Baseline at Turn 0:** 100% (baseline assumption of authority)

**What Decreases Institutional Trust

**Plague Deaths:** -2% per 10,000 deaths

- Each city losing 50,000 to consumption = -10% Trust
    
- By Turn 20: If 2-3 major cities affected = 15-20% Trust lost already
    

**Failed Policy Responses:** -10% per failed strategy

- Aromatics fail (Turn 20): -10% Trust
    
- Moth control fails (Turn 60): -10% Trust
    
- Each failed escalation adds -5% more
    

**Resource Wastage:** -5% per massive cost with minimal benefit

- Massive aromatic spending (Turns 10-20) then aromatics fail: -15% Trust
    
- Moth control spending (Turns 35-50) then fails: -10% Trust
    

**Authority Collapse Events:** -15% per major crisis realization

- Aromatics failing unexpectedly (Turn 20): -10%
    
- Moth theory being wrong (Turn 60): -15%
    
- Cascade event occurring (Turn 60): -20%
    
- **Cascading realization that authorities don't understand = -50% Trust in one turn possible**
    
**What Increases Institutional Trust

**Establishing Plague Doctor Department:** +20%

- Visible, professional response
    
- Demonstrates government is taking action seriously
    
- Flavor: "The learned physicians have established their guild in the capital"
    

**Building Quarantine Centers:** +5% per center

- Stacks with each additional center
    
- 4 centers in different cities: +20% cumulative
    
- Physical manifestation of government control
    

**Successfully Implementing Visible Policies:** +5-10%

- Food security measures showing food still available: +5%
    
- Infrastructure hardening preventing cascade damage: +10%
    
- Each visible success rebuilds credibility
    

**Establishing Harmonic Guardians Institution:** +25%

- Major shift from "we don't understand" to "we've figured it out"
    
- Credibility peak moment
    
- Flavor: "The Harmonic Guardians have come forward with the solution"
    

**Successful Crisis Transition:** +30%

- Turn 75+: Authorities have successfully guided civilization through crisis
    
- Saturation stabilized: +15%
    
- Population loss below 50%: +15%
    
- Full recovery to 100% Trust only if Age of Behemoths achieved.

|Trust Level|Population Behavior|Policy Effectiveness|Consequence|
|---|---|---|---|
|80%+|Full cooperation|100% effectiveness|Quarantines work, people follow advice|
|60-80%|Partial compliance|70% effectiveness|Some people ignore warnings, partial quarantine breaches|
|40-60%|Significant resistance|40% effectiveness|Many people flee, quarantines fail, policies sabotaged|
|20-40%|Widespread defiance|10% effectiveness|Riots possible, authority ignored, civil chaos|
|Below 20%|Authority collapse|0% effectiveness|Government overthrown, complete chaos|

**Cascading Trust Consequences

**Trust Below 50% during Turns 50-75:**

- Quarantine Centers stop working (people breach)
    
- Additional population loss: +1-2% per turn (panic flight)
    
- Institutional Trust drops further: -1% per turn (negative feedback loop)

**Trust Below 30% during Turns 60-75:**

- Riots occur in major cities
    
- Additional population loss: -5% (one-time from riot violence)
    
- Institutional Trust: -15% (massive failure)
    
- Government legitimacy questioned
    

**Trust Reaches Below 10% (Rare):**

- Government overthrown
    
- Civilization fragments into independent city-states
    
- Age of Embers guaranteed (cannot recover unified civilization)
    
- Scenario becomes: "Dark Ages, City-State Fragments" outcome

**METRIC 3: Population Morale (Civilian Happiness)

**Measurement:** Civilian happiness/satisfaction percentage (visible on UI)

**Baseline at Turn 0:** 100%

**What Decreases Morale

**Plague Deaths:** -0.5 per death (cumulative per city)

- 10,000 deaths in a city: -5,000 morale (spreads to adjacent regions via refugees)
    
- Significant but not catastrophic
    

**Visible Policy Failures:** -5% morale per failed response

- Aromatics fail (Turn 20): -5%
    
- Moth control fails (Turn 60): -5%
    
- Cascades kill people despite promises of safety: -10%
    

**Crisis Events and Cascades:** -10% morale per major cascade event

- First cascade (Turn 60): -10%
    
- Subsequent cascades (every 2-3 turns): -5% each
    
- By Turn 75: Morale hit -30 to -50% from cascades alone
    

**Restrictions and Hardship:** -1-5% per turn for each restriction

- Quarantine (reduced movement): -3% per turn (but worth it for disease control)
    
- Reduced extraction (less magical benefits): -2% per turn
    
- Food rationing: -5% per turn (only if food shortage, can be prevented)
    
- Curfews/martial law: -7% per turn (desperation measure)
    

**Euphoria Debuff (Turns 60-75):** +20% morale (this is the trap)

- Masks underlying morale collapse
    
- Creates false sense of everything being fine
    
- When euphoria wears off (Turn 75), morale crashes hard
    
- Post-euphoria morale: actual underlying morale level (likely 20-40%)
    
**What Increases Morale

**Community Infrastructure:** +3% morale per building

- Hospitals: +5%
    
- Shelters: +3%
    
- Religious sites (temples): +5%
    
- Food stores: +5%
    

**Visible Disease Reduction:** +10% per manifestation declining

- Consumption cases dropping: +10%
    
- Dancing Plague cases declining: +10%
    
- Cascades stopping: +15%
    

**Government Faith Initiatives:** +2-5% per turn

- Prayer services: +2%
    
- Religious celebrations: +3%
    
- Miracle rumors: +5%
    

**Successful Policy Implementation:** +5% per visible success

- Food becomes available again: +5%
    
- Infrastructure repaired: +5%
    
- Magical balance restored: +10%

|Morale Level|Behavior|Consequence|Policy Impact|
|---|---|---|---|
|80%+|Cooperation and hope|Population accepts hardship, follows policy|Policies 100% effective|
|60-80%|Cautious compliance|Some resistance but mostly cooperative|Policies 70% effective|
|40-60%|Significant resistance|People ignore policies, some flee|Policies 40% effective|
|20-40%|Widespread rebellion|Quarantine zones breached, riots likely|Policies 10% effective|
|Below 20%|Civilization breakdown|Revolution, society fragments|Government overthrown|

**Morale Below 60 during Turns 50-75:**

- Quarantine zones experience breach attempts
    
- Each breach: -0.5% population (escapees)
    
- Authorities must increase enforcement (Curfew policy): -3% morale per turn to prevent
    
- Catch-22: Preventing breaches requires harsh measures that lower morale further
    

**Morale Below 40 during Crisis:**

- Riots begin in major cities
    
- One-time population loss: -5% per riot (each major city affected)
    
- Infrastructure damage from riots: -10% per riot
    
- Cannot be prevented, only managed
    

**Morale Below 20:**

- Civilization fractionalizes
    
- Central authority loses control of regions
    
- Each independent region has separate morale
    
- Coordinated crisis response becomes impossible

**Managing Morale: The Difficult Balance

**Strategy 1: Restriction (Works But Costly)**

- Quarantine: -3% morale per turn, but -30% disease spread
    
- Net: Morale loss is temporary (worth it), disease control is worth it
    
- Duration: Turns 50-70 (20 turns), cumulative -60% morale if only measure used
    
- Must pair with hope-giving measures to survive
    

**Strategy 2: Hope-Giving (Works But Slow)**

- Religious initiatives: +2-5% per turn
    
- Visible infrastructure improvements: +5% each
    
- Problem: Slower than morale-damaging events
    
- Rate: Religious services +2% per turn vs. disease deaths -0.5% per death per 10,000
    
- By Turn 30: If 100,000 deaths across civilization, disease losses = -5%, but 10 religious services only = +20% partially offset
    

**Strategy 3: Balanced (Works But Requires Both)**

- Restrictions for disease control (painful but necessary)
    
- Plus hope-giving for morale (slow but necessary)
    
- Plus successful policy implementation for credibility (builds trust, which builds morale)
    
- By Turn 75: Morale can be managed to 55-60% range

**METRIC 4: Magical Saturation

**Measurement:** Magical saturation level in Dual Confluence Stream (0-100 scale)

**Baseline at Turn 0:** 5

**Visibility:** Hidden until Turn 60, then fully visible

**Saturation Accumulation (Without Mitigation)

**Baseline Increase (Every Turn):** +1 per turn

- Normal civilization operation
    
- Cities using magic for construction, agriculture, energy

**Growth Bonus (If Pursuing Heavy Magic Use):** +2 per turn additional

- Building more magical infrastructure
    
- Using magic for warfare/expansion
    
- Pursuing magical technologies aggressively
    

**Repair Attempts Post-Cascade (Turns 60+):** +1 per repair attempt

- Each time authorities fix cascade-damaged extractors: +1 saturation
    
- Vicious cycle: Cascades damage infrastructure → need to repair → repair requires extraction → extraction raises saturation → more cascades
    

**Catastrophic Growth (Turns 60-70):** +2-5 per turn

- Cascades themselves releasing magical energy
    
- Euphoria overflow feedback loop
    
- System racing toward critical threshold


**Saturation Reduction (With Mitigation)

**Reduced Extraction Policy (Manual Management, Turns 50+):** -1 per turn

- Player deliberately reduces magic use
    
- Costs: -20% production (magic-dependent infrastructure suffers)
    
- Effectiveness: Slow but reliable
    

**Harmonic Guardians Institution (Turns 60+):** -5 per turn

- Automatic regulation
    
- No micromanagement required
    
- Costs: -20 production per turn maintenance
    
- Effectiveness: Much faster than manual
    

**Aetherlight Prism (Relic, Turns 50+):** -10 per turn

- Absorbs excess Aetherlight
    
- Costs: 400 production + 50 Aetherlight to build, -10 production/turn maintenance
    
- Build time: 3 turns
    
- Effectiveness: Very fast, but resource-intensive
    

**Lunehymn Vault (Relic, Turns 50+):** -10 per turn

- Absorbs excess Lunehymn
    
- Costs: 400 production + 50 Lunehymn to build, -10 production/turn maintenance
    
- Effectiveness: Mirrors Aetherlight Prism
    

**Harmonic Resonator (Advanced Relic, Turns 55+):** -15 per turn

- Balances both resources actively
    
- Costs: 600 production + 100 both resources, -15 production/turn maintenance
    
- Build time: 5 turns
    
- Effectiveness: Most powerful but most expensive

Survivors experience:

**STAGE 2: False Hope Collapse (Wave II Breakthrough)**

Post-plague theology diverges by zone:

- **Moderate-saturation zones** (secondary cities; trade routes): Theology of witness and presence; Auroral Ribbons pilgrimage becomes dominant spiritual framework
    
- **Low-saturation zones** (refuges): Mixed; some cling to Auric Aria faith; others join pilgrimage; philosophical diversity
    

**Narrative Implementation**:

Different survivor archetypes create distinct narrative branches:

- **The Hollow/Sacrificer**: Elara template; surrenders to emptiness; becomes Atonalis
    
- **The Angry/Revolutionary**: Seeks systemic change; potentially becomes antagonist to Lacrimosa cultists

# Hollowmarch

#society #religion

Originally known as the Golden March until it swapped names to Hollow during [[The Hollowing]] and in its aftermath.

One of the key societies in [[Arcanoria]], the first classical [[Civilization]] founded by [[Aurelian]] and [[Daedalus]] in the [[Great Expanse]] on the west of the central continent of [[Arcanoria]]. It was established as a safe-haven of [[Humanity]] and [[Demi-Human]]s under the light of the [[Auric Aria]]. Formally, it is known as the "Empire of Laureated Marble" given the aesthetics of white and gold that permeate most of society.

This empire is the cradle of the [[Auric Order]] and it's the largest empire of the [[Ages]] of Foundational Magic. Its foundation begins in [[Ages]] I, and carries itself until the modern era in [[Ages]] XI but with many societal transitions, the most important of these events is [[The Hollowing]] after [[Hollowmarch]] becomes the crown of [[Lacrimosa]] during the [[Age of the False Messiah]].

The most notable of its [[World-Bending Relics]] is the original [[Auric Bell Staff]] of [[Daedalus]] as the first of the [[Auric Bells]] ever made.

During [[Ages]] V, they become a major player alongside [[Iridia]] during the [[Holy War]] crusades as [[Hollowmarch]] becomes the head of the theology anew in renewed [[Auric Order]] fervor after surviving [[Lacrimosa]] and the [[Atonalis]] Reign.

# Hypermage

#chaos #technology

_"The manmade horror version of Prismo. A god made hive mind in a lucid stasis dream."_

An impossibly large [[Megastructure Wonder]] of nested [[Consciousness]] composed of [[Spellweaver]]s where each become one neuron within a large matryoshka style brain. This is one of the most advanced possible combinations of [[Spellweaving]] and the end point of going against the [[Weight of Nature]] by creating an emerging [[Consciousness]] through a man-made god where each individual [[Spellweaver]] [[Consciousness]] is a neuron to the [[Hypermage]]. It works through the layering of several [[Hyper Chord]]s in impossibly advanced combinations to stabilize, this layering is what gives the [[Hypermage]] its name. The emerging [[Consciousness]] of [[Hypermage]]s varies greatly in their design but the standard follows three rules:

- **[[Strand Pool]] stasis dream pods:** The first part is creating the tomb containing all of the individual [[Spellweaver]] bodies that consist of [[Flux]] + [[Strand]] + [[Luminance]] + [[Crystal]]. These are the individual encapsulation pods that contain and connect the brains of each [[Spellweaver]] by embalming their bodies within the requiem fluid chamber of the [[Hypermage]]. It's the final state that puts the individual [[Consciousness]] in a state of a perpetual dream stasis that surrender their human existence into individual neurons for the emerging [[Consciousness]]. _"Humans are to the [[Hypermage]] what cells are to our own body. They exist independently only to make the collective sentient."_

- **The [[Flesh-Casing Ritual]] [[Flux]]-[[Crystal]] mind cables:** The second [[Hyper Chord]] is a [[Crystal]] + [[Flux]] + [[Luminance]] + [[Resonance]] combination where they connect the brains of each [[Spellweaver]] through [[Crystal]] and [[Flux]] conduits serving as the medium of [[Stable Harmonic Channels]] while the information of each individual [[Hypermage]] neuron is channeled and connected through a combination of [[Luminance]] for the [[Frequency Harmonics]] of their brainwaves and synchronized by a giant [[Resonance]] field. This allows the data of each individual brain to function at a micro and a macro level simultaneously, surrendering the individual [[Consciousness]] in favor for the emerging hive mind. Any [[Hypermage]] starts by linking at least 100,000 [[Spellweaver]] [[Consciousness]].

- **The [[Strand]] [[Superposed Resonance]] Anchor:** To final and most complex part to really power up the amount of [[Consciousness]] to unimaginable levels is to cause a state of [[Superposed Resonance]] in the hive mind by utilizing [[Strand]] to create a closed [[Time Bubble]] where every infinite point taken between 0 and 1 by creating an iterative loop of folding [[Probability Amplitudes]] of [[Consciousness]]. The spell functions by layering [[Strand]] + [[Resonance]] + [[Void]] + [[Cindergale]]. This requires a continuous hum of a self sustaining power loop by sacrificing individual [[Hypermage]] neurons in the infinite moments right before the present, and using the indefinite infinity to layer mirror images in a [[Void]] beneath the [[Hypermage]]. This requiem chamber exhibits a continuous hum of [[Superposed Resonance]] that uses [[Cindergale]] to permanently function on itself. It creates a [[Time Bubble]] paradox where the hive mind is sacrificing its entire self the moment just before, right on collision and dissipation into [[Primal White Noise]] and the infinite futures where such didn't happen. This layering is the hardest part to achieve and is where most [[Hypermage]]s meet their end before generating an emerging [[Consciousness]] able to warp reality. It turns the individual 100,000 [[Consciousness]] into infinite copies of itself.

- **Additional [[Atonalis]] anomalous properties:** Most [[Hypermage]]s require the integration of [[Atonalis]] into their collective by facilitating the stability of [[Resonance Anchors]] through the introduction of anomalous properties. It serves on the principle that "a small dose of poison is a strong antidote" to stabilize the highly impossible [[Hyper Chord]]s routing [[Consciousness]].

A [[Hypermage]] is considered a highly dangerous mass suicidal ritual that surrenders the individual [[Consciousness]] in favor of a massive emerging man-made god that is able to drastically alter reality. These are usually considered genies because they can only grant so many reality bending wishes until they collapse due to the sustained friction of layering three or more highly advanced [[Hyper Chord]]s. They use the [[Consciousness]] contained within itself to balance this state of stasis but it can only be done with much difficulty. As result, this creates an unimaginable almost alien "requiem construct" by using each individual [[Consciousness]] in favor of the emerging hive mind [[Consciousness]] that is no longer human, gaining properties unique to the new [[Weight of Nature]] of the [[Hypermage]]. Their very presence is a [[Scorching Truth]].

### The Nature of Wishes of [[Hypermage]]s

As [[Hypermage]]s are impossibly alien constructs, they operate on a [[Luminance]] interface similar to that of [[The White-Haven Library]]. This means that to direct any of the command spells of the [[Hypermage]] it is necessary to use the nature of [[Soul Leitmotif]] wishes, which is precisely what gives the reputation to [[Hypermage]]s of being "cosmic genies." However, just like with the real-life fairytale, the exact wording of the wish is crucial for harnessing their power as it is highly likely that the phrasing of a wish lacks the [[Sufficient Precision]] required for it to collapse with [[Absolute Certainty]] and the sheer scale of reality bending capabilities tends to create hyperboles of said wishes, and unintended side effects.

Moreover, a [[Hypermage]] is not truly omnipotent, it requires a certain wish to have constrains on the way it is worded before proceeding to execute it based on how likely is the wish to manifest, this is effectively its [[Coherence]]. This happens because a [[Hypermage]] doesn't have the ability to rewrite all laws, and the more "omnipotent" the wish, the more engineered the [[Hypermage]] has to be, increasing the lower limit of the initial number of nested consciousness infinite fold, instead of 100,000 to grant further reality bending capabilities without drawbacks it would require 10,000,000 or more. As such, this is why every wish has a set of [[Coherence]] required to execute, and why it's necessary to find workarounds to get the exact desired outcome.

For example, the looping wish of [[The Ultimate Weapon]] is caught precisely with the middle of both ends. It had to be engineered to create a looping paradox instead of "find the perfect timeline" because the structure was decaying and having a wish like "remove all suffering" or removing any of the [[Seven Weights]] is an omnipotent power even beyond the [[Auric Aria]]'s capabilities as creator goddess. Thus, it had to compromise with unintended side effect of scrambling the timeline with [[Crisis Wonders]] compounded from the poor infrastructure, the result of the lack of [[Sufficient Precision]] and the desperate attempt it has to reboot reality to fulfil the wish. This is a result of equal parts the decaying infrastructure of [[The Ultimate Weapon]] as much as it is the result of the compromising wording of the wish itself.

# Imperfection of Life

#scorchingtruth 

A [[Scorching Truth]] based on the [[Weight of Flaw]] which details that the true [[Perfect Manifestation of Life]] is impossible, nothing is immune from cruelty, from sorrow, from suffering, either as victim or as perpetrator. Neither the most gentle pacifist nor the greatest, enduring creatures are safe from it. It is the birthright of all [[Consciousness]] to wither, to eventually perish, either by the harsh hand of violence or by a withering death in time. The cycle is inescapable as it is as true as life itself.

Neither [[The One True God]] or any [[Outer God]]s can change it despite how much they would desire to reshape reality. Existence and [[Consciousness]] is flawed and we are all powerless to the cruel [[The Infinite Void]]. [[The Eternal Symphony]] itself is a requiem for all life, and for there to be a requiem something has to die first.
